utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-75-T, the Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Prosecution, Alex Demirdjian with Lisa Biersay, Thomas Laugel, our case manager; and our legal intern, Agnes Bugaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Defence of Goran Hadzic, Zoran Zivanovic and Christopher Gosnell. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: There is a short oral ruling we could deal with. The Prosecution filed a motion for order requiring redaction of certain portions of the public transcript of GH-080 and 038. Is there any -- anything from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: There is not, then the motion is granted. The witness may be brought in. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Before we do that, Your Honours, do you remember you wanted to discuss the issue of timings?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We had announced nine hours for this witness. I announced to the Defence that I may be going a little bit over that to ensure that I have covered all the topics, so I may be an extra hour. So that means that, roughly speaking, I should be finished by the end of the second session more or less today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. First of all, we have no objection to that request for additional time. And if you're asking for an estimate from the Defence on the cross-examination, we initially had estimated nine hours, so equal to what had been requested by the Prosecution. I think that that is still probably a valid estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Roughly that should work for -- to be able to finish this witness by -- after the Monday hearing. So that's good. Thank you. If there's nothing else, the witness may be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We left off yesterday with the war diary of the 80th Motorised Brigade, if you will remember. And the war diary indicated that the security for the camp at Ovcara was withdrawn and that it was replaced by the Vukovar Territorial Defence. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, keeping in mind the warning that we saw earlier which was issued by the 1st Military District on the 18th of November with respect to acts of retribution and revenge by the Territorial Defence, how do you assess the decision to have the security detail withdrawn and to leave it to the Vukovar TO?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course when we -- I mean, when I would answer that question, there are different ways of looking at it. You can look at it now with hindsight where obviously -- I mean, the answer is clear knowing what has happened, but even at the time of the events, i.e., prior to the crimes that occurred in Ovcara, there is a contradiction between on one hand the order of the command of the 1st Military District to prevent such acts and to maintain JNA control in the area and on the other hand to hand over prisoners to members of the local Serb TO, including volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now at the time this area was still under Operative Group South's area of responsibility; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was located in the area of responsibility of OG South.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, with respect to the -- if you remember we saw the order on the evacuation -- well, the order which included a sentence with respect to the evacuation on the morning of the 20th of November which was issued by Mile Mrksic. Now, considering the character of the evacuation, the way you described that yesterday, who can decide on the situation where prisoners had to be handed over to another unit?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, given the organisation of the forces in the 1st -- in the area of Vukovar, I mean JNA forces and forces operating under JNA command, the order should have come from the -- would have come from the 1st Military District to OG South and then OG South to its subordinate units. And the 1st Military District would have acted upon the instructions of the Supreme Command through the staff of the Supreme Command which was -- where General Kadijevic was the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, as of page 485 of your report you explain that with the end of combat operations a number of orders were issued with respect to the resubordination of certain units, including the Territorial Defence. And perhaps it would be useful at this stage to look at 65 ter 658 which is at tab 188. And in your report this is at the bottom of page 485, it's OG South order number 464-1. Right. Now we see this is dated the 21st of November at 6.00 in the morning and the title is: "Regulating the Issue of Resubordination and the Return to Home Units." Now, you've dealt with this order in your report. Could you give us briefly your view of what would -- what's its significance in the context of the events?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the significance is that after the events in Ovcara in the late afternoon and evening of the 20th of November, on the 21st of November, so the morning after at 6.00, an order is issued by OG South command to resubordinate Leva Supoderica volunteer detachment or TO detachment from the Guards Motorised Brigade from assault detachment in the Guards Motorised Brigade under which it was subordinated until then to another unit, namely, the 12th Mechanised Brigade of the 12th Corps and also some other units are being moved. And in the -- I mean, what is -- I will only talk about the paragraphs that are relevant in relation to the question. Paragraph 4 then adds that Vukovar TO units will be resubordinated to the 80th Motorised Brigade because they were prior subordinated to the Guards Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We can look at the diagram in your report so if you can -- sorry --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you. It's also useful to look at the list of addressees at the bottom of the document because I think it supports some of the points I have mentioned in the previous days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That would be on page 2 in the English version and page 1 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to draw Your Honours' attention to the fact that, I mean, in an official JNA document mention is made of a Seseljevci volunteer detachment highlighting actually the link between these volunteers and Mr. Seselj, i.e., the Serbian Radical Party and the relations between these volunteers even when they're operating under JNA command and Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation, Mr. Theunens. If we can return to the expert's report which is at 65 ter 5988 and in the English version go to page 587 [sic]. I don't have the specific B/C/S page number but it should be around 550 or 551.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 487, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: 487 in English, yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I see it is recorded as "587." I meant to say "487." Thank you. Thank you. And here the title or the description you've given to this graphic is that it's a representation of OG South number 464-1, which is the one we just saw; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. And this is a diagram I drew, so it's not part of the order but it's my interpretation of the order. So we see the move of Leva Supoderica which used to be part of OG South, and we have seen in prior orders that they were part of I believe the 1st Assault Detachment --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- of the OG South. And through this order they move from OG South to the 12th Corps, more specifically the 12th Brigade, and then the TO Vukovar which used to operate under -- again in assault detachments commanded by officers of the Guards Motorised Brigade in OG South they are resubordinated to the 80th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In B/C/S it's page 550. And with respect to this scheme or this graphic representation we have in front of us, could you tell the Court for how long does this remain in place?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it starts in the course of the 21st of November as is indicated in the order 464-1 and it lasts until -- well, the next order. I believe there is an order in -- is it in end of November or early 1992 concern -- for the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade in relation to resubordination of the TO Vukovar -- I mean in the meanwhile, of course, the Guards Motorised Brigade leaves by the 23rd of November in the evening and there is also a later decision I think that's from January 1992 where Mr. Hadzic requests I think the JNA 1st Military District to disband Leva Supoderica. But that's much further -- that's a new document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Just before the graphic -- if we can scroll down just a little bit, please, there's a letter (d) so we can see it in full. You have a comment here that the 1st Military District order, and you give the specific number 115-151, is not recorded in the war diary. Now, is it correct to say that at the time that you drafted this report in the Mrksic case that document was not available to you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. And notwithstanding that we requested it because as part of the military analysis task when you see references in one order to other documents, you obviously want to see these other documents because they provide context. And 115-151 of the 1st Military District dated 20th of November, 1991, was not available to me prior to October 2012.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The -- can we then look at 65 ter 657 which is at tab 508. This is a document which is not in the report, Your Honours. Now, we see here that this is a document to the 1st Military District. Do you see the confidential number?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So this is the one that we were just discussing, 115-151. Very well. So this is a report on the results of the combat operation. It's issued on the 20th of November. And I'd like to take you to the second paragraph below the subject, so it's the one starting with "under the single command ..." Looking at this paragraph here: "Under the single command of the JNA, units of the 12th Corps, TO detachments from Serbia and Vojvodina, with many volunteers taking part, freed tens of thousands of residents of Vukovar ..." et cetera, et cetera. Do you have a comment with respect to this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. I mean, it's consistent with what you have been looking at all the previous days, i.e., that there is single and unified command over the forces operating on the JNA side whereby they operate under the command of the JNA during combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And on the last paragraph of this page the first sentence says that: "All the Serbian populated areas south-east of Osijek are under the control of the forces of the JNA, TO, and volunteers ..." So is this a reflection of the situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Objection, that calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I apologise. I'll rephrase the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, based on the information that you have available and the documents that you have reviewed, how does this representative of this situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, I have to object. That does call for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just -- we are asking that the expert gives his appreciation based on the documents that he has reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, the specific question was: Does that reflect the situation on the ground? The question wasn't if those are the facts, what consequences are there, what is the implication, how does it reflect chain of command, and so forth. So I do believe that the question is calling for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You may answer the question, Mr. Theunens, based on the documents you consulted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Based on the documents I reviewed, Mr. Panic confirms that Eastern Slavonia is under the control of the JNA and the forces operating under its command and control during combat operations. I think -- I mean, Panic gives a summary of the -- or a description of the current situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if we go to the last page -- well, the next page in the English version and both -- also in the B/C/S. Do you see the sentence before in the last one which starts with: "I give full recognition to all officers, soldiers, conscripts and volunteers for the successes achieved in combat." Do you see that sentence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We will deal with this in more detail with another document, but at the time what was the appreciation, perhaps, or -- of the value of the volunteers in the combat operations?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, as well as in other documents, and I believe it's included in the amalgamated report, there was also a statement by General Mrksic published in the bulletin or in an article "Narodna Armija," so the JNA official magazine where he praised and other senior officers praised the efforts and the contribution by the volunteers. There may be a reference here in the document -- in the report, but there is also the visit on the 21st in the morning by a delegation of the Guards Motorised Brigade and people like, if I'm not wrong, Miroljub Vujovic and/or Stanko Vojnovic of the TO Vukovar, and they are also linked to the SRS volunteers are also invited to the reception with Mr. Kadijevic in Belgrade. I mean, they are part of the delegation of the Guards Motorised Brigade that is invited to the reception in Mr. Kadijevic's office in recognition of their victory in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, this issue of the reception in -- by Kadijevic is dealt with page 489 of your report. Since it's there, I will not deal with it in much detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document we just looked at is not in the report. It was 65 ter 657, tab 508. Might I apply to admit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1694. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, at page 490 of your report and 491 as well, you explain that as of the 23rd of November the 80th Motorised Brigade takes over the command of Vukovar and that the colonel of the 80th Motorised Brigade, the commander, Colonel Vojnovic becomes the town commander of Vukovar. So this is based on again the military documents and orders that you have seen; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours, and the orders -- the process is described -- the process of hand-over of authority from the Guards Motorised Brigade to the 80th Brigade is described in the report because the Guards Motorised Brigade returns to Belgrade, whereas the 80th Brigade stays in the wider Vukovar area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So I'd like to move now to this issue of the town commands which you deal with at page 491, and before we get into the specifics perhaps can you give the Trial Chamber a bit of doctrinal background as to what the town commands are, what they consist of.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the contemporaneous reference documents as -- concerning the role of town commands -- no, I would rephrase that. Apparently there is a reference to the town commands in the 1985 rules of service in the JNA where reference is made to garrison commands, but for one or the other reason I didn't have that available at the time. But the specific orders during the October/November time-period, orders from the 1st Military District, and also instructions from the SSNO explain the role and the functions of a town command. And basically those role and functions correspond with those of the civilian authorities, which means that a military authority takes or assumes the role that should normally be fulfilled by civilian bodies of authority in the absence of functioning civilian bodies of authority or, as we also see in these documents, in the absence of recognised civilian bodies of authority. There are bodies of authority -- civilian bodies of authority present already earlier in Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem, when I mean "earlier," you have the whole process of establishing SAO SBWS authorities. But it's only on the 20th of November that the 1st Military District issues a document, this is a new document, this is 2436-1, whereby it explicitly recognises bodies of the SAO SBWS as the competent bodies of civilian authority. This is not the case prior to the 20th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We will look at that document in a moment, but just before that in the context of the Vukovar operation, could you tell the Court when do town commands start to be created?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is already -- I mean, it's on page 491, Your Honours, there is already an order from the 1st Military District, 1614-82/27, where he mentions -- General Panic orders basically his subordinate commanders to establish full control in the zone of responsibility and pay special attention to the functioning of military authority. And then -- I mean, this is followed on the 9th of November by an order by the command of OG South. This is 349-1 and it corresponds with footnote 1434, where Colonel Mrksic organises a number of town commands, for example, in Negoslavci, Ovcara, Jakubovac, Grabovo, Barek, and other locations, and there's subsequent documents so I think it's pretty clear in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. So this one here that we're looking at on the screen now, the 9th of November, it is in your report and -- well, I see a typo there, the date of 9th of November, 1001, should be probably corrected to 1991. It is also on our list as 65 ter 552 just for the record. May I ask that we display -- yes, it's an admitted exhibit, P365, please, it's at tab 556. Now, Mr. Theunens, I'm going to ask you to look at one of the new documents that we obtained last summer. Now, you see that this is issued by the command of the 12th Corps on the 8th of November, so this is the day before the Mrksic order we just saw. Now, do you see at the bottom of the page -- well, first of all, in the initial paragraphs again you have an explanation of the situation. At the bottom of that page there is a question: "To what extent should we observe the actions of the ... Serbian district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem and the government of that district, which in fact exist ...," et cetera, et cetera. Now, this is a military document issued by the 12th Corps. What is your assessment of the question that is put here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I mean by that time these -- the bodies I mentioned earlier, these self-declared bodies of civilian authority of the autonomous Serbian district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem exist and they try to influence the situation, they even try to exercise authority. And this question indicates that there is no clarity yet as of -- in relation to what attitude the JNA is to adopt towards these bodies, whether they have to consider them as recognised bodies of civilian authority or not. And so the Chief of Staff of the 12th Corps asks for clarification, but he's a bit kind of suggestive in his question in the sense that he also expresses that -- I mean, his personal views, i.e., that they have already established what he calls the legal legitimacy and even legitimacy at the international level.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: 12th Corps at the time was, as we saw at the top of the document, was headquartered in the village of Dalj. If we stay on the same page in the B/C/S version we need to go to the next page in the English version, there is yet another question here. And it's the first bullet point at the top of the page which reads: "To what extent should we recognise the Territorial Defence of the Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem SO, which is connected to the government?" And then we see a suggestion, I believe, in the next paragraph. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, so far the majority of the documents that we have seen are reports, orders, et cetera. How do you view a document of this nature which is basically going up the chain of command seeking guide-lines?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it's not an unusual the situation. I mean, the command of the 12th -- as you expressed the forward command post of the 12th Corps is in Dalj. The 12th Corps and its subordinate units are operating in the northern part of Eastern Slavonia and they are confronted or they notice the existence and maybe certain activities of organs associated with or linked to the SAO SBWS. And obviously -- I mean, the military is not fighting 24 hours on 24. Once an area has been captured or the JNA and its subordinate forces have achieved control over this area, then there is requirement to return to, I would say, normal life and to allow the people who are still staying there to go on with their daily life. And ideally these kind of aspects are managed or even organised by civilian authorities. 12th Corps sees that there are such self-declared civilian authorities, and on one -- on the other hand, I mean there are orders of General Panic to enforce military control as the one we discussed earlier. So they seek clarification from General Panic as to how they should approach and which attitude they should adopt towards these self-declared SAO SBWS authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In the next paragraph the Chief of Staff here of the 12th Corps suggests that the Territorial Defence, as it has been formed in SBWS, should be fully disbanded and a new one should be formed. Do you have an explanation as to why this suggestion would have been made?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the only document that discusses this aspect at that moment in time. There are various explanations possible. I mean, looking at the overall context and other not necessarily military documents but other sources of information, there is no clear structure and it's a lot of ad hoc arrangements based on the few men that are available. Some units are stronger, some are weaker because of the lack of resources, or some other units have more resources. There is sometimes political affiliations and so on that play a role, so it's all very ad hoc and not necessarily in accordance with the regulations as they existed in the SFRY armed forces. So one option is that indeed General -- Colonel Trajkovic, sorry, wants to start with a clean table or suggests to start with a clean table and then establish a local Serb TO in accordance with the rules as they have been set in SFRY armed forces doctrine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you to look at the document you referred to earlier, this is at 65 ter 6026, tab 558. It is a new document and this is the document you refer to as 2436-1.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm sorry, for the record this document was already admitted as D19. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you see the document in front of you, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you mentioned the number 2436-1 earlier. Is that -- is this the one that you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. As indicated, this is a new document and I find -- I consider it a key document because for the first time, again based on the documents I have reviewed, the commander of the 1st Military District explicitly identifies organs established by the SO or SAO SBWS -- I mean civilian organs, I'm sorry, civilian organs established by the SAO SBWS authorities as competent organs of civilian authority. Prior instructions or previous instructions by Panic did not mention the SAO SBWS, but, for example, used terminology like "self-declared bodies of civilian authority" and always insisted on not recognising these bodies and preventing them from interfering in the daily activities while emphasizing the importance of the military through the town commands of taking care of the tasks that would normally be carried out by bodies of civilian authority. So that's why it's a key document, in my view.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Looking at item 2 here, the fourth bullet point or dash states that: "The task of the local commands is to," amongst other things, "work to establish civilian authorities in municipalities ..." And here we see in parenthesis that it makes reference to a decision of the SO SBWS with respect to the municipalities. I want you to go to the next page in both versions at item 6.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean just to come back what you say about paragraph 4. It states indeed that the -- I mean, Panic clearly states that the established organs of authority are those that have been established by the SAO or the SO, the Serbian Ooblast, Serbian district of Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And can you offer us a comment with respect to paragraph 6 which states that: "Co-operation with the Government of the Republic of Serbia and the S AO ... will be ensured by the command of the 1st Military District ..."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it makes sense because the 1st Military District -- sorry, the 1st Military District remains in the area and it's an implementation of the principles of command and control.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. I'd like to -- sorry --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean just to be complete. So the highest level -- I mean, the military district co-operates with the level of the SAO, and then the subordinate units, they will co-operate with the lower levels, including the municipal organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. That's the next sentence at item 6. Is that what you're pointing to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I was pointing at to show this division of labour. But in order to ensure -- I mean, not just consistency but basically single, unified command and control.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: At page 494 of your report which in B/C/S is page 558, you make a reference to an interview with Colonel Vojnovic and it's a reference to interview of Vojnovic as a -- as the town commander of the town of Vukovar. And this is, I believe, recorded in one of the SSNO bulletins which we also have as 65 ter 566. Now, I believe it is on -- yes, on page 495 of the English version, please. So you have here the interview with Colonel Vojnovic and -- sorry, in B/C/S it's probably 559. Thank you. Do you see the second paragraph which reads: "In carrying out this task, the Army has been co-operating with the government of the Serbian region, its ambition not being to take over or retain power in that territory, further stated the Vukovar town commander." How does this compare with the documents that we have seen so far?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document -- this statement is consistent with the instructions given in the order 2436-1 by the commander of the 1st Military District on the 20th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And on the next page at 496 of your report, which should be 560 in the B/C/S version, you say here that -- well, you make a reference to an instruction of the 27th of November, numbered 588-1. And you say here that this order establishes the bodies or organs of civilian affairs in the military units. Could you briefly explain to the Trial Chamber what was the role and function of this -- of these organs of civilian affairs?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The organs of civil affairs or civilian affairs, as defined in the instruction 588-1 from the SSNO basically take care of, yeah, civilian tasks -- I mean, all aspects of civilian life. For example, re-establishing -- sorry, providing assistance to re-establish infrastructure, providing assistance in relation to management of abandoned property, resettlement of population, and other aspects of civilian authority, as they are explained in the first paragraphs of this instruction. They also address I think in paragraphs -- I mean, when you look at the document 1, 6, and 8 the issue of protection of the civilian population. And I mean, a more detailed description can be found in paragraph 4 of the instruction. And again they highlight or they explain how co-operation should be organised with the local civilian authorities, and this is done in paragraphs 2 and 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, this -- this instruction is included in your report, it is also, for the record, at 65 ter 2919. And it is correct to say that this instruction is followed by a second one a few weeks later, and this is at page 500 of your report. And this instruction is numbered 588-3. Can you tell us what is the significance of this instruction?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before answering the question, obviously when you have 588-1 and 588-3, the question is: What about 588-2? But this document so far is not available. It -- I don't think it was included in the new documents that were obtained. 588-1 and 588-3 were obtained at the time prior to the Vukovar trial when we requested the authorities of the Republic of Serbia for any documents that regulated the relations between the military and self-declared civilian authorities in the conflict areas in Croatia. And to answer the question, 588-3 contains more details in relation to the tasks that have been enumerated in 588-1. And again, it's all aspects of civilian authority, administration, legislative tasks, and judicial and executive authority, protection of civilians, and so on, always highlighting the supporting role of the military, of the JNA, in relation to these tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, at page 501 of your report you refer to a Memorandum of Understanding of the 27th of November, 1991, and at this stage I would like us to have it on the screen. It is 65 ter 722 at tab 211.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry, could I ask for a reference, a 65 ter reference, in respect of --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That would be 65 ter 708 at tab 207 of our list.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you see the memorandum before you, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, we see a number of names on this page from various organs and institutions, and if we scroll down to the bottom of the page we see a number of members of international organisations. Before we look at the details of this document, could you perhaps give us the factual background surrounding the reaching of this Memorandum of Understanding?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is basically a Memorandum of Understanding between officials of FRY -- SFRY -- sorry, it should be SFRY instead of FRY, the Republic of Serbia and Croatia, and the JNA. And it, as I put in the report, it formalises their commitments towards the role and activities of the ICRC and the strict application of all four Geneva Conventions. So it's a totally different matter from town commands, but it's more follow-up on the issue of the treatment and the handling of prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, this was a -- yes, the date is, I believe, we will see it later, on the 27th --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yeah. If we turn to page 2 in both versions, what do we find in a nutshell on this page?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's -- I mean, I think it's a reiteration of the relevant and the applicable Geneva Conventions concerning the treatment of prisoners of war; the treatment of civilians, i.e., the protection of civilians; and also how hostilities should be conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, this -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Including the wounded and the sick, but I mean it's obvious on the screen, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, it is right there on the screen. You conclude at page 504 of your report that the signing of this Memorandum of Understanding - and there's a subsequent SSNO memo - these are directly related to the events that have occurred during and subsequent to the evacuation of the hospital in Vukovar on the 20th of November. And this was also directed to the way OG South had handled the evacuation. Could you perhaps explain to the Court how do you reach that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from a chronological point of view obviously one can establish that the events in Vukovar and the evacuation of the hospital and so on precede the signing of this memorandum. There is, of course, also - which is not mentioned here in the report but somewhere elsewhere - the 23rd November cease-fire agreement. It was well-known that there were disputes or -- in particular among the JNA about the nature of the conflict whether it was an international or an internal armed conflict. And so it would make sense to have this memorandum then, to clarify the responsibilities of -- clarify the responsibilities -- I mean, first of all, the understanding and then the ensuing responsibilities of all sides in relation to, yeah, the protection of civilians, the handling of wounded and sick, and also the handling of prisoners of war. Most obviously it doesn't refer to what happened in Ovcara in the evening, but it's -- if there is a link, I mean, the link I identified was more to the handling of the evacuation of Vukovar Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, we will be going to a different part of your report. Before I do that, you did mention yesterday that an international agreement had been reached between Slobodan Milosevic, Franjo Tudjman, and General Kadijevic in Geneva and that was on the 23rd of November; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a cease-fire agreement had been signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If we could display 65 ter 699, which is at tab 669, please, and the reference to this is on page 146 of the report.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the record this is Exhibit P1344.1325. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, looking at the first page we see the date here, the 24th of November, there is a letter that is addressed from the Secretary-General. And could we go to the next page. We see that the letter here is signed by Javier Pere z De Cuellar. And if we can move to the next page, which is the annex. At the bottom right we see Geneva, 23 November 1991. We see a number of signatures. And we see the agreement here, "the undersigned agree ..." So first of all, we see that Croatia agrees to lift the blockade of all JNA barracks and installations in Croatia and that the JNA will, with immediate effect, begin the withdrawal from Croatia of personnel, weapons, military equipment in those barracks and installations, et cetera. And then we have unconditional cease-fire. Now, this was on the 23rd of November and I believe you mention that this was followed in your report with what had became to be known the Vance Plan; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. On the 2nd of January there is a subsequent meeting in Sarajevo, where the parties agree for further cease-fire as well as the plan that became known as the Vance Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So we'll discuss the Vance Plan now. We are at page 210 in the English version of your report and that's page 250 in the B/C/S version. Now, here you introduce the context of the signing of the Vance Plan, and if we look at the next page you describe the three phases which are included here. Could you just summarise it for the Trial Chamber before we look at more specifics.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the first phase consists of deploying what was described as a lightly armed United Nations peacekeeping force, UNPROFOR, the United Nations Protection Force, together with unarmed observers, UNMOs, as well as a United Nations Civilian Police Force, UNCIVPOL, in three areas in Croatia which are identified as the UNPAs, United Nations Protected Areas, and these three UNPAs are organised in four sectors: South, north, west, and east. And the definition of the UNPAs can be found in the report. The second phase is the withdrawal of all armed forces, i.e., the demilitarisation of the UNPAs and the control of the demilitarisation of the UNPAs which doesn't only imply the withdrawal of the JNA and the ZNG as we have seen earlier, but also the disbanding, demilitarisation, demobilisation of the weapons -- of the -- excuse me, of the local Serb SAO SBWS as well as the SAO Krajina and by that time we're talking about -- oh, no, we're not yet talking, sorry. I thought we were already talking about the RSK bu the RSK does not yet exist. Sorry. But so the disbanding, demilitarisation, and demobilisation of local Serb armed structures, whereby the weapons are put under a so-called dual-key system, that is, that the weapons in -- I mean the storage sites -- both UNPROFOR and the local Serbs have a key to these storage sites. And the third phase consists of the maintaining of peace in the UNPAs in order to prepare for the return of refugees and also create the conditions for political negotiated solution of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: On the next page you describe the establishment of the UNPROFOR on the 21st of February, 1992, and this is followed by a section where you deal with the attitude of the RSK towards the Vance Plan. Now, you explain here that on the 2nd of January the RSK proclaims a constitution of the Republika Srpska Krajina and that Article 102 declares the Territorial Defence of the RSK as the armed forces of the Republika Srpska Krajina. And you conclude here that having regards to the Vance Plan this decision was -- you consider it to be a violation of the Vance Plan. Now --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I write "it can be considered a violation," it's not that I consider it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: "Can," thank you. Now, were there any subsequent efforts to correct the situation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, summarising the events between January and November 1992, actually the opposite is happening because first we see that with the assistance -- or actually with the -- based on the orders of the SFRY or what remains of SFRY armed forces, a local TO, an RSK TO, is established. And then this TO is largely transformed into special police units, also known as the PJM. And then starting in May 1992, but actually being let's say fully implemented by November 1992, the RSK establish an SVK, so the armed force or the Army of the RSK whereby PJM units which were in fact re-batched TO units are transformed into units of the SVK. It doesn't mean that all the police is transformed into the military but those units PJM which were in fact re-batching or restructuring of TO units are transformed into SVK units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You make a reference to a number of documents to that effect, and to illustrate what you just told us, I would like you to look at one of the new documents we obtained last summer which is 65 ter 6104 at tab 609. Yes. Do you see the cover page here which starts with "I approve" and it's commander Major-General I think the name is not legible but it says the command of the 1st Proletarian Guards Mechanised Division, and there is a stamp at the bottom, 24th of February. And what this is we'll see on the next page, page 2 in English and B/C/S, it says it's a Work Plan of the command of the 1st Mechanised Corps on the preparation of units to receive the United Nations forces. That's February 1992. Now, first have you had an opportunity to review this document, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I mean, I've seen several Work Plans because this is a regular kind of document issues by corps and even I think by brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In the English --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the JNA. Sorry, the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I apologise, yes. In the English version could we move to the next page, please. We can stay on the same page in the B/C/S version. I'm not sure if it's very visible on the right side of the screen for you -- yeah, thank you. That might be a little better. You see under item -- well, we don't see it quite yet. Yes, with a bit of creativity we got there. Now, you see item number 1 which includes -- well, the title: "Strengthening of Combat-Readiness." And if we scroll down to item 2 it deals with the formation of TO units. And you see that the completion date here is 20-25 February, there's a colonel who's in charge, and the fifth column -- maybe can we just scroll up to the fifth column to see the title of that. Yeah. The title says "collaborators," and if we move down again we see commander of the TO of the SAO SBW -- SOS BZS. Now, what is your view on this -- first of all on this section which says "formation of the Territorial Defence units"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this is what I meant by the JNA based on instructions given by the SSNO assists in the formation of at that time RSK TO units, including in the SAO SBWS.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if we -- in the English version if we can move to the next page. In the B/C/S I think you only need to scroll down. It's item number 3. Yes. Yes, in the English can we scroll down a little bit. Do you see the title here: "Receipt and distribution of weapons and equipment and recruitment reviews." And we see that the person in charge we have commanders of the 1st mK, 80th mtbr, and Colonel Miljkovic. What is your comment on this item?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this item shows that the assistance that is provided in relation to establishing TO units in the RSK including SBWS also involves weapons and -- I mean, there's other documents talking about ammunition and other military equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, the following pages contains an enormous amount of detail we don't need to really get into.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honours, this is 65 ter 6104. It is a new document and we would seek to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1695. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we display on the screen Exhibit P171 which is at tab 596. It is also one of the newer documents. Thank you. Your Honours, I notice that this is an admitted document but that the header hasn't been translated on the left-hand side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Theunens, are you able to see at least in the B/C/S version who is initiating this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It comes from the 1st Military District and -- I mean, we would see -- have to see at the end who signed it. Yeah, this is the chief -- I mean, yeah, the Chief of Staff of the 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, if we look at the substance of the document, it deals with a meeting which took place on the 24th of January, 1992, between representatives of the 1st Military District and representatives of the government of the region of SBWS. And at the meeting the 1st Military District was represented by a couple of corps commanders while the Serbian district was represented by the prime minister, the minister of internal affairs, the minister of people's defence, and the Territorial Defence staff commander. And here we see: "The objective of the meeting is to discuss issues in the development of the police and the Territorial Defence in line with an agreement dated 17th January 1992." Now, can you provide us your comments again with respect to the issue of development of the police and Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again it's consistent with, I mean, the various documents discussed in my report in relation to that. It is from the highest level SSNO. Instructions are given to the JNA to provide assistance in establishing and organising TO units as I mentioned earlier but also RSK police units, I mean at this stage -- yeah, RSK police units. And this assistance consists not only of like what I would say plans and policy, i.e., how to set up a unit, how to manage it, all the regulations and doctrine that apply to that, but also effective support consisting of weapons, ammunition, military equipment, vehicles, and all that is needed to establish functioning TO and police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask you to look at another document which is 65 ter 6144 at tab 361. This is one of the new documents. Now, this one appears to be dated the 18th of November, 1992. We see the header here Republic of Serbian Krajina, district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, and it is issued by the Mirkovci municipal staff of Territorial Defence. Now, Mr. Theunens, if you look at the first paragraph -- and just before that you see it is sent to all Mirkovci municipal TO. It says here that: "Pursuant to a decision of the government of the district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, the command of the Territorial Defence district staff issued the order to establish special police units whose basic and main task is to provide security for the border with the Republic of Croatia." Are you able to give your assessment of what is exactly happening here with this decision?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is what I would call the second phase in the process, referring to my earlier answer where the first process was the assistance by the JNA to establish local Serb TO and local Serb police, and this is happening in the time-period January to -- let's say to March 1992 in view of preparing for the situation when the JNA has officially withdrawn. The second phase being the transformation of at least a number of TO units because they are actually prohibited by the Vance Plan. When I say "prohibited," I mean they should be demobilised, demilitarised, and disbanded. So this provision of the Vance plan is circumvented by transforming these TO units in special police units also known by the acronym PJM, and I mean this is maybe -- no, still interesting to note is, I'm sorry, that is that they talk about the border with the Republic of Croatia. When you look at the Vance Plan, the Vance Plan does not attempt to draw a conclusion as to whether the territories controlled by the Serbs or the parts of Croatia controlled by the Serbs should stay under Serbian authority or whether they -- I mean it doesn't state that so it is a bit unusual to use terminology like the border with the Republic of Croatia because it is not a border.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is one of the new documents. Might I propose to tender it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1696. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, at page 214 of your report you're dealing with this establishment of police brigades and PJMs and you indicate that JNA and RSK TO commanding officers and other personnel as well as JNA and RSK TO equipment are transferred to the newly established milicija brigades of the RSK MUP. And on this topic I would like you to look at one of the new documents which is 65 ter 6165 at tab 645. Yes, thank you. We see that this is a document of the 252nd Armoured Brigade command and it is dated the 9th of April. And it is delivered to the 1st Mechanised Corps. Now, very briefly, would this brigade be a unit as part of the 1st Mechanised Corps? Are you familiar with this unit?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honours, indeed. I mean, it's -- obviously it's a JNA unit and it's at that time present in the area of Eastern Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, what we see here is the title: "Report on the Selection and Appointment of Officers to Command Duties in Police Organs." And we have a Jovan Stevic here, a lieutenant-colonel in the armoured mechanised unit. We see his military occupation, date of birth, et cetera. And that he has expressed the wish to be appointed Chief of Staff of the Vukovar police brigade with the establishment rank of lieutenant-colonel. Again, what can you tell us about this proposal or this expression of interest?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, among the new documents I reviewed in September 2012, there were several documents from the JNA on one hand asking for volunteers, asking subordinate commanders to check with unit members whether they wanted to remain in Baranja or Eastern Slavonia or Western Srem and on the other hand you have also expressions of interest by members of the JNA to remain in the area, irrespective of the fact whether or not they were born there or not because Gnjilane is obviously not in SBWS. And it shows that actually JNA officers could then -- I mean, if his application was approved, be appointed to a senior position in a local police unit and there's no indication that any specific training or education was required or would be given in order to facilitate that transfer from the JNA to the SBWS police/milicija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I tender this document? It's one of the new documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1697. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, with respect to this topic there are several other documents. I have selected two which I would propose to tender without necessarily having to go into the details. I don't know if you would prefer for me to display them on the screen very briefly. They are two documents that are exactly of the same nature, of the same topic, of expressions of interests from JNA officers to move into police brigades. So the two documents -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: If they are really similar and the Defence agrees that they are similar, then I think we can use the rule we already had at previous occasions. Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps in fairness to the Defence I can quickly show them on the screen to make sure this is what I'm claiming that it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The first one is 65 ter 6166. And it is at tab 646 of our list. So as you can see, Your Honours, it is another document from the brigade going to the 1st Mechanised Corps, we see a name, and if we scroll down there is an expression of interest to be appointed as chief of communications of the Vukovar police brigade. So that's one of them. Does the Defence have any objection on this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, as long as the witness says that these documents are similar or the same or connected, that would be sufficient for us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This is a similar example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1698. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And the second one is 65 ter 6173 at tab 651.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And perhaps, Mr. Theunens, a brief comment on this one because this time it's not going from one of the brigades. It's issued by one of the corps and it is addressed to the 1st Military District. Could you briefly describe what we're looking at here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a summarising document, i.e., it's not a JNA officer who expresses his interest -- I mean I would say on a personal basis, but this is a summarising or this is actually an overview document, the list compiled by the 1st Mechanised Corps which was -- which chose to be if I'm not -- sorry, the 1st Mechanised Corps which is then forwarded to the 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if we could look at the second page in the English version, yeah, you see a number of other names here.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, and it concerns officers and NCOs, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well and this is --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, and just to highlight, they're not necessarily born in SBWS or in other parts of Croatia, but you see people born in Pristina, which is in Kosovo, or Belgrade or Loznica, so they are -- I don't know which criteria were applied in order to allow JNA personnel to remain in SBWS, but it's not just an issue of having been born there which has often been mentioned in the past. I mean, in the context of this also people who went to serve later in the SVK, that, well, you know, they were born there so they wanted to protect their homeland. This doesn't apply obviously to all of them given the fact that they were also born outside Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I offer this document as well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1699. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, if we move to -- yes, it is at page 211 of your report when you were mentioning the UN protected areas you explain here that these areas were supposed to be demilitarised according to the Vance Plan. And in connection with that I would like you to look at another document which is 65 ter 6190 at tab 660. Thank you. Now, we see that this is a document issued by the Federal Secretariat of National Defence and it says JNA's operations group for Sarajevo with UN peace forces, are you familiar with this unit or this organisation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I've seen it on the document. It's -- if I -- my recollection it's a liaison element of the JNA, I mean it -- by that time we have actually already the VJ, but maybe this is an old heading or an old stamp they are using in the absence of updated stamps because by June 1992 SFRY doesn't exist anymore. We have the FRY. And, yeah, there is an element, a liaison element of the VJ with UNPROFOR, among others in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, we see here this is dated the 18th of June, and the first two paragraphs deal with what is said here to be a violation of the truce by the Croatian side. And that the Krajina TO responded to the fire and repelled the attack. However, later the Krajina TO forces opened fire with 120-millimetre mortar and, according to claims of the Croatian side, on several locations. Now, can you tell us, first of all, what type of weapon is this, 120-millimetre mortar?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, a mortar is an indirect fire weapon. I mean, 120-millimetre you could consider -- it's to be considered a heavy mortar which in accordance with the provisions of the Vance Plan it should have been withdrawn or kept in a warehouse under dual key, i.e., UNPROFOR and the local Serb TO in Sector East. So it should not have been used. I mean -- and none of the parties should have opened because there was also a cease-fire, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And here there is an indication that the opening of the fire from 120-millimetre mortar in this phase is a serious violation and that the information was forwarded to the Lieutenant-General Nambiar with the liaison officer, and it would be reported to New York and New York would report it to Belgrade. I would like you to look at the last sentence in this report which says: "We recommend that the competent authorities and organs of the Krajina TO be told at all levels about how damaging this conduct is." Can you again give us your comment about what is meant here about the damaging aspect of this conduct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's what I just said, the use of a heavy weapon is a violation of the provision of demilitarisation and also the provision of cease-fire included in the Vance Plan. I mean, traditionally this would be reported by the UN UNPROFOR troops in Sector East to the headquarters in Zagreb. General Nambiar was the force commander and he would then inform UN headquarters and UN headquarters would raise it with -- yeah, in this case Belgrade; in case of a Croatian violation, they would raise it with the Croatian side. And at the same time, the parties can also send letters of complaint to the United Nations which would have to be investigated then in order to verify whether a claim is justified -- a claim of a violation order unallowed unauthorised behaviour is justified, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is one of the new documents. It's 65 ter 6190. Can I apply to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1700. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, with respect to the previous sub-issue where you were discussing the fact that some officers of the JNA and the TO were transferred into the RSK police units, you make reference to this at page 289 of your report. I would like you to look at -- well, also at page 214, actually, because they're in both places. I would like you to look at a document you cite in your report which is 65 ter 1151 at tab 292. Very well. We see that this is a document of the 2nd of June, 1992. It's issued by the cabinet of the president of the RSK. And the title says: "Proposal for Promotion Submitted to the Presidency of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia." Now, we see the name here Borislav Djukic, an infantry colonel. We see -- well, what is next to his rank, VES 31040, are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure anymore whether it's his personal military number or his military -- I mean, the number of the position he's occupying, because I understand during the events -- I mean, end of 1991 he was a brigade commander in the 9th JNA Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And do you see here under "currently," it says that he is performing the duty of commander of the Special Police Units of the milicija in MUP RSK. Now, how does that compare to what you told us with respect to the earlier documents we saw?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, Colonel Borislav Djukic is one of the examples of senior officers who were transferred from the JNA first into the RSK TO and then in the RSK PJM where in this case he's appointed commander of the PJM.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if we can go to the next page in the English version. Yes, we can scroll down to the bottom of the page in the B/C/S version. Very well. Now, we see that this document is issued by the president of the government, we see the name of Zdravko Zecevic, the minister of internal affairs, and we see the president of the republic Goran Hadzic. And I'd like to ask you here if you remember on the cover this proposal was sent to the Presidency of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Do you have an explanation or a comment with respect to this?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is just, Your Honours, an implementation of doctrine because promotion of colonels to generals is the prerogative of, yeah, the Presidency of the republic. I mean, whether it was in SFRY or in FRY, it's the same. And since he is, in fact -- even if he's serving in the RSK TO and subsequently in the PJM, Colonel Djukic is, in fact, a JNA officer or by that time a VJ officer. So it's up to the FRY authorities, i.e., the Presidency, to promote him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is not a new document. I guess we can deal with this with our filing in a week or so. I believe that the Defence has expressed that they don't have an objection with contemporaneous documents, but we'll deal with that in our motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, if it helps we wouldn't object to this document coming in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, is it practical at all to tender it now, to have it admitted now, or do you wish for us to leave it all in one package?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We would have prefer to have it in one package, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, very well. I believe it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It is, indeed. Mr. Theunens, our first break. We'll come back at 11.00. The court usher will escort you out of the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian -- oh, the witness of course. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'm going to press the pause button on the topic that we've been dealing with so far and I will ask you to do some mental gymnastics with respect to an issue that we were dealing with yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 669 on the screen which is at tab 171.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If you remember, yesterday we were dealing with the end of the operations in Vukovar and we were looking at some of the agreements relating to the evacuation. Yes, this is the document that we were looking at. This was the bulletin, if you will remember. And if we could go to -- in the English version to page 2, the bottom of the page, I'd like to have a little clarification here. Yes. Could you look at the -- yes, the bottom of the page where the issue of the signed agreement was dealt with. If you remember yesterday your comment was that you would need to see other evacuation agreements to reach a certain conclusion. Now, with respect to the signed agreement that is referred to here, could you look at the last sentence. We did not deal with it yesterday. And it says here that: "A new agreement was subsequently reached with Croatian authorities to evacuate civilians, wounded, and sick on November 21st, 1991." Now, what is your comment with respect to the fact that first there's a discussion about a signed agreement and then there's a discussion about a new agreement on the 21st?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, at face value the use of the expression "new" would suggest that we are talking about a different or -- if I would call the signed agreement the first agreement in the context of this paragraph, then the new agreement would be a second agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And have you seen other evacuation agreements besides the Zagreb or Raseta Agreement?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my recollection, Your Honours. I mean, I've seen references to various agreements, but no -- I don't recall seeing other signed agreements.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I would like to show you two documents which I apologise to say I didn't have -- I didn't show you during proofing and you can take your time to look at them on the screen. The first one - and we've advised the Defence that we will be showing this document - the first one is 65 ter 631. And you can see that it is dated November 20th, 1991, in Zagreb. And at the bottom of the page we see Colonel Imra Agotic. Are you familiar with this name?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Colonel Imra Agotic was a JNA officer who served in the air force and air defence corps and he left the JNA, if I'm not mistaken, in the course of 1991 to join the Croatian defence forces or the Croatian national guard. And he was at that time the counterpart of the General -- or the Colonel Andrija Raseta we mentioned yesterday, so he was the senior negotiator involved in exchange of prisoners of war, or matters related to evacuation of Vukovar similar to General Raseta but this time on the Croatian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And if I pause after your questions it's simply because I've been reminded to do that during the break.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can you look at the first sentence which refers here to an oral agreement reached on November 20th --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: -- about the transfer of wounded and ill from Vukovar Hospital and the refugees convoy from Vukovar, et cetera. And there is a suggestion here to receive these convoys in Bosanska Raca. And if you look at the bottom of the page there is I believe what is a suggested route which -- I mean, could you tell us very briefly these towns that we see are Bosanski Samac, Orasje, Brcko, Bijeljina, where are these located?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are located in -- I'm sorry. They are located in northern Bosnia in an area which became known as the Posavina corridor, I mean Bosanski Samac and Orasje and Brcko. Bijeljina is in north-eastern -- main city in north-eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And I'd like us to look at another document which follows this one, it's 65 ter 5116.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I must have seen this document during the nine years I worked here, but -- or the eight years I worked here, but I don't think I discussed that in one of the reports or at least not the Vukovar report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the document to come up. Thank you. Now, we see here it's written at the top: "To the Government of the Republic of Croatia, Zagreb, November 21st, 1991." Now, we've mentioned him before. We see that it is signed by General Lieutenant-Colonel Andrija Raseta and again the first sentence is a reference to the verbal agreement reached on November 20th, 1991, and the agreed proposal route. He mentions also Bosanska Raca and we see the third paragraph there is a reference to Bosanski Samac as well. So again, with respect to these two documents and the SSNO bulletin that we saw earlier, does this clarify a little bit what was the reference to the signed agreement?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, but this talks about a verbal or an oral agreement, so I'm not clear whether there's a reference to a written agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And I apologise. My question may have not been clear. In the first document we saw the SSNO bulletin there was a reference to a signed agreement.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And at the time you -- yesterday you told us that you were not able to reach any conclusion as to which signed agreement this was a reference to and that you needed to see if there were any other agreements.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: These agreements we see here on the first document. It says oral agreement. Here we see verbal agreement. So my question to you is: Are you able to reach a conclusion as to which agreement the SSNO bulletin was referring to when it said the signed agreement?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, no, because unless I can establish that the only written agreement is the Zagreb agreement, I cannot answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And have you ever seen any other signed agreements --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: -- on the evacuation of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. So I mean I could say that the signed agreement has to be the Zagreb Agreement, but of course that could be challenged if another agreement could be -- would be shown to me, but I'm not aware of any other agreement so -- I mean, I could answer assuming that there is no other written agreement then the Zagreb is the written agreement that the SSNO makes reference to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, these two documents were not on the list; however, just for the completion of the record I would seek to tender them, 65 ter 631 and 5116, to complete the record on the questions that were dealt with yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter document 631 shall be assigned Exhibit P1701 and 65 ter document 5116 shall be assigned Exhibit P1702. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now we will return to the topic we were dealing with before the break which was the transfer of JNA and TO officers to the RSK MUP units. Could you look at the next document which is on my list, 65 ter 6185 at tab 657. Now, Mr. Theunens, this is one of the, again, new documents that were obtained last summer. We see here that the header is from the 1st Mechanised Corps command on the 20th of May, 1992, and the report relates to the status of units and police stations in the corps' area of responsibility. Now, do you see on page 1 if we scroll down at item 1 here there's a discussion here about the five police stations being established, Vukovar, Ilok, Mirkovci, Orolik, Tovarnik, et cetera. And if we turn to page 2 only of the English version, we can stay on the same page in the B/C/S version, there are numbers here under item (b) establishing -- first of all, under item (a) you have the manpower, and under item (b) you have the MTS levels. I think we've seen this term before but very quickly what does that refer to, MTS?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: MTS stands for materiel equipment, so I mean you see it with the subtitles, weapons, communication equipment, vehicles, uniforms, and other supplies, I mean materiel equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'd like to take you now to page 3 which is page 2 in the B/C/S version. And if you look at the second paragraph it reads here that the 1st Mechanised Corps command has extended assistance and armed the peace time establishment police structure in Mirkovci and Orolik with long barrels, loaned them wire communications and other equipment. Do you have any comments with respect to the assistance provided here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's consistent with the documents we have seen before, I mean which are cited in my report in relation to the assistance that is provided by the SSNO in establishing a local Serb TO and also a local Serb police and the instruction of the SSNO are then obviously implemented by the subordinate units of the JNA in their respective areas where they are deployed, in this case the 1st Mechanised Corps in Eastern Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In the English version if we turn to page 4, I think in the B/C/S version we can scroll down to the bottom of that page -- no, we will need to go to the next page in B/C/S as well. I'd like you to focus on item 7. Here there is a mention to: In the area of responsibility of the 1st Mechanised Corps, there are cases and tendencies of establishing own militias. Are you familiar with this situation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
