utterances.text: Your Honours, among again what I would call the new documents, those that I could review in September 2012, there is a whole range of documents consisting of reports by organs of civil affairs of the JNA, including also assistant commanders for civil affairs of the JNA units that are still present in Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, and Western Srem and there is a pattern where they highlight that there are shortcomings in the functioning of the SAO SBWS local authorities, which become part of the SRK local civilian authorities, including also the existence of so-called uncontrolled armed groups or groups that are not necessarily co-operating with the JNA or have been established with JNA support, but maintain relations with members of the local Serb civilian authorities. And according to the JNA reports are involved in activities in criminal activities like looting or harassment of local civilians and so on. And this is an example concerning the establishment of police units where there are also apparently parallel or de facto armed structures or self-styled structures like here in Mirkovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And I apologise, I missed an issue on item 5. Could we return to page 3, please. Yes. Item 5, you see here that it says the: [As read] "Regular police staff have been recruited from the ranks of Serbia MUP who have sent a core of men on a temporary assignment ..." Have you seen other documents which relate to this issue?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have. I cannot recall exactly which documents at this stage, but I also know from my previous work outside ICTY that there was a presence of members of the Ministry of the Interior or the police of the Republic of Serbia among the RSK MUP in Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem which is quite logical given that they are, I mean, neighbouring areas which is very easy to send personnel from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a new document 6185. May I tender it, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1703. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: On the same topic if we could look at 65 ter 6191 which is at tab 661. Yes, very briefly, this is a document of the state of the police in the Mirkovci village, and you see here that they are reporting pursuant to the plan of work of the 1st Mechanised Corps command's plan of -- work plan, basically. And in the English version I'd like to take you to the second page on the top of the page. And do you see the sentence here which states that: "The personnel allocated on a temporary basis from the Serbian MUP are expressing dissatisfaction with the whole system of organisation ...," et cetera. So is this again another document you have seen in reviewing your documents?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, it's one of the new documents and I think I've answered the question before. There are members of the police of the Republic of Serbia who are serving in the RSK police or milicija in SBWS on a temporary basis, and there are several documents showing that these members of the MUP Serbia are not always happy with the fact that they are temporarily reassigned to the RSK or to SBWS.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. That's the only matter I wish to explore in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: May I tender it, Your Honours, it's 65 ter 6191.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1704. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, could I take you now to page 369 of your report, where you discuss the RSK Law on Defence of the 23rd of March, 1992. In B/C/S it's page 420. And -- yes. Here you highlight the adoption of the RSK Law on Defence and I believe you focus here on Article 5 on this page and Article 6 on the next page. Now, looking at Article 5 first, it focuses on the fact that the RSK armed forces are considered to be part of the SFRY armed forces. Now, if you remember a moment ago we looked at the constitution which was adopted on the 2nd of January, 1992, which provided for the creation of a Territorial Defence of the RSK. How does that compare with the terminology here, the "RSK armed forces"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean the Law on Defence further specifies issues related to the armed forces as they have been defined in general terms in the constitution. So it further clarifies the concept of armed forces by stating that in certain conditions the special purpose units of the police would be integrated in the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if we go to the next page where you're dealing with Article 6 --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, and I could just add that it shows actually the military nature or the paramilitary nature of this special police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. And here at Article 6 you're dealing with the powers of the president, which include that the president leads the armed forces in peace time and in times of war. And we also see at item number 5 that he orders the use of the police in times of war, in times of imminent threat of war, and states of emergency. Now, am I correct in saying that a year later in 1993 this power of the president does change a little bit with the creation of the Supreme Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours, with the amendments in 1993 to the RSK constitution and subsequent Law on Defence an RSK Defence Council is established, whereby it is stated that the president leads the armed forces in accordance with the constitution and the decisions of the RSK Defence Council. And obviously the president is a member -- one of the five members of the RSK Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We will hopefully, if time permits, look at that amendment, but it is in your report in April of 1993. You describe elsewhere in your report that the RSK is created -- sorry, the -- just a moment, please. You discuss the establishment of the SVK at pages 388 onwards, and -- yes, and it's at page 389 -- well, let's look at it now, 389 is where you deal with the amendment adopted pursuant to a decree -- I'm sorry, I may have the wrong page here. Yes, I apologise. It's at page 296 of your report, which in B/C/S is 342. Now, here on 296 we see that the RSK Supreme Defence Council is created by a decision of the 20th of April, 1993, and you indicate that the Supreme Defence Council is composed of the RSK president, the prime minister, the minister of defence, the minister of interior, and the commander of the Serb Army of Krajina. So I know we're jumping ahead in time a year later, but can you tell us with respect to the RSK Law on Defence of 1992 how it is impacted by this amendment?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- I mean, the -- as I mentioned, the introduction of a Supreme Defence Council could be seen as curtailing the powers of the president because instead of being the supreme commander on his own, now he commands the armed forces in accordance with the constitution which obviously was obviously the case but also with the decisions adopted by the Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, based on the documents that you have reviewed, what were the president's power with respect to the SVK?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, he's the supreme commander so he's the highest political authority and he -- I can repeat myself for a third time, but ... I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps let me clarify it, yes. Perhaps the question would be: In practical terms how did that transpire?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we've -- I mean, he commands the armed forces in accordance with the constitution and the decisions of the Supreme Defence Council. He can promote people. He -- I mean, he has the last word when it comes to issuing political decisions in the manner as I have expressed, so other detailed responsibilities can be seen in the relevant articles.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at a document which you have reviewed, it's 65 ter 5352 at tab 540. You see on the screen that this is an UNPROFOR document and I'd like us to go to page 2, please. You see here that it is signed by Lieutenant-General Lars-Eric Wahlgren, force commander. Are you familiar with this name?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. He was the force commander of UNPROFOR at that time, so not only the UNPROFOR forces in Croatia but the overall commander because at that time also -- I mean forces in Bosnia -- peacekeepers had been deployed in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Returning to page 1, we see here that the letter is addressed or begins with: Dear Mr. Hadzic, and what is happening here is that he informs or wishes to bring to the attention of the president a serious humanitarian matter. It is the shelling of civilian targets in the territory of Croatia, et cetera, et cetera. What I'm interested in is not specifically the events described in the document but your assessment of the UNPROFOR commander sending a letter to the president of the RSK, how do you assess that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it -- it's a logical move because the president of the RSK is the supreme commander of the armed forces of the RSK, I mean based on the constitution, so de jure. And the fact that General Wahlgren sends a letter to Mr. Hadzic shows that also for Mr. Wahlgren, who may well not be hundred per cent familiar with the applicable legislation in the RSK, for Mr. Wahlgren, Mr. Hadzic is the supreme commander, is the highest political authority who also decides about the use of the armed forces in the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And just to complete the topics, if you go to page 2, the last sentence here says that: "I am also writing to the other party to this conflict in request of breaches emanating from their military activity." Now, is that consistent with the events at the time, based on the documents that you have reviewed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't analysed in my report the nature of hostilities between Croatia and RSK in that period of time, but I am familiar with the fact that there was mutual military activity or mutual violations of the Vance Agreement occurring between let's say -- the adoption -- I mean the earliest -- the adoption of the plan until, actually, the Operation Storm in August 1995. So on a regular basis there was military activity by both sides that resulted in violations of the Vance Plan as well as is highlighted here, the targeting of civilian objectives, in this case by forces of the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a new document. May I offer to tender it, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1705. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, we dealt earlier with documents, instructions number 588-1 and 588-3 which dealt with the relationship between the 1st Military District and the Serb regional district in SBWS. I would like you to look at a document which is a new document, 65 ter 6154 at tab 637, please. Yes, it's 6154, that's what I said on the record. Sorry. Thank you very much. Now, this is a document of the 1st Military District dated the 27th of March, 1992, and it is sent to the 1st Mechanised Corps and the 12th Corps. Here we see that the requesting information to carry out an initiative for attaching an organ of civilian affairs to Executive Councils as a group of advisors, and based on the request of the SSNO they are requesting the following information for the command, and a little bit lower they are asking for proposals to ensure that a group of advisors is assigned to the Executive Council. I would like you to comment on how do you assess the use of the word "advisors" in this context?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, this is in line with what I said earlier, that after the 20th of November the role of the JNA in relation to exercising civilian authority changes, and whereas prior to the 20th of November, 1991, the town commands, JNA town commands, are in charge. After the the 20th of November, 1991, the JNA through the bodies for civil affairs fulfils a supporting and advisory role to the civilian bodies of authority of the SAO SBWS, as is the case also in other parts of Croatia which are by then under Serbian control. But I mean I reviewed only the documents that covered Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all I have for this document, Your Honours. May I tender it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1706. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the town commands, Mr. Theunens, could you generally tell the Court what type of matters were they reporting about to their superior authorities? And just to be clear, I meant to their superiors within the army chain of command.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand. I mean, again, as I mentioned earlier, within the group of new documents, I mean those that became available to me in October 2012, a very large number of these documents consist of daily or weekly reports by the organs of civil affairs, whereby they report on the functioning of the local Serb civilian authorities, addressing areas like, for example, the treatment of abandoned property, the treatment of civilian population, in particular non-Serbs. In some cases there are reports on criminal activity on -- also on the lack of functioning or problems with the functioning of SAO SBWS local civilian authorities. So it's mainly these areas that are being covered in a regular manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the first topic that you mention, the treatment of abandoned property, I would like us to look at 65 ter 6048, which is at tab 570.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It could very well be that I'm causing the trouble. Please try again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It's working now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If we look at this document, Mr. Theunens, it is a 1st Military District document from the 11th of December, 1991, and I'd like us to focus on the first paragraph here which states that: "Some commands have received requests from certain local officials for making use of abandoned property and farms. It refers to collecting unharvested crops, abandoned cattle ..." et cetera, et cetera. Item 1 here states - and again this is from the 1st Military District, that: "All ... issues should be resolved in co-operation with and at the request of government officials of the Serbian district ..." and in parenthesis here there's a comment that "all government officials carry special ID to prove their actual position." Now, first of all, can you offer us your comments with respect to the issue of dealing with abandoned property in co-operation with the Serbian district?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This paragraph shows that the government officials of the SAO or the SO, it's actually the same, Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, and Western Srem, they have the lead and the JNA has an advisory or supporting role. So the decisions are taken by members of the SAO SBWS authorities, civilian authorities, and the JNA then assists by that which is consistent with other documents from the SSNO as well as -- or the other documents from the SSNO as well as the 1st Military District that are released after the 20th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if you look at item number 3 here it says that: "In order to prevent any allegations linking the JNA and its members with possible abuse of abandoned property, the following should be done ..." And there are three steps here. First: "Local authorities are in charge of managing locally abandoned properties and it is their obligation to create records ..." Second step: "If local authorities do not exist, but a government commissioner is present, it is the local command that manages the property in agreement with the government appointed commissioner ..." Just to clarify here, are you aware of what the term "local command" refers to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the local JNA command, so the unit in which zone of responsibility the property is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if we turn to the next page in the English version and that would require us to go on the next page in the B/C/S version as well, you see the third dash: "If neither the local authorities nor the government commissioner exist, it is the local command that makes the decision in consultation with the local assembly ..." et cetera. First of all, on these three dashes, these three points we've seen, do you have any comments on how this issue is supposed to be dealt with by the local commands?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it's all consistent in a sense that the local civilian authorities have the lead unless there are no local civilian authorities and then only then the JNA takes over, summarising these three scenarios that are described.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Scrolling down to the bottom of that page if you can look at item number 6, again there's a reference to "local commands," and it is instructed here that they shall honour Municipal Assembly decisions, Executive Council decisions, and the decisions made by the government of the Serbian district. Now, is this again consistent with the instructions 588-1 and 588-3?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly, and it -- sorry, and it's also consistent with the 1st Military District order 2436-1 from the 20th of November as well as the subsequent orders that figure among the new documents and probably you will address later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now -- yes. And -- sorry. Yes, this is a new document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It's 6048. Your Honours, may I apply to tender it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1707. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I would like you to take a look now at 65 ter 6056, which is at tab 578. Thank you. We see this is a document issued by the command of the town of Ilok on the 23rd of December, 1991. And it says here that it's a regular daily report submitted to the 1st pgmd. I'm interested in item number 10 which is on the next page. So after reporting on the situation to the 1st pgmd, here there is a comment that: "Occupation of empty houses continue in the territory of the command of the town of Ilok's area of responsibility. Occupation is done without knowledge or approval of the command of the town of Ilok. The Presidency of the SAO Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem has not given an announcement so far regarding the way and conditions of occupation, which places this command into a very complex situation." And then he ends with: "At the same time ethnic Croatian inhabitants are under pressure to leave this territory." Now, this is one document. Have you seen other reports dealing with the same topic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have, Your Honours, and actually there are several topics. There is, first of all, the topic or the issue of the reoccupation of abandoned houses and farms and land. I mean Eastern Slavonia was a very fertile area. And secondly, there is also the topic of the presence of minorities of non-Serbs, including ethnic Croatians, but I've also seen documents on pressure -- I mean according to the JNA pressure exercised to -- against Ruthenians or Ukrainians in parts of Eastern Slavonia to encourage them -- or Hungarians to encourage them to leave. And this pressure is exercised -- I mean in a number of documents members of the local Serb authorities are identified as being behind this pressure or at least supporting it or failing to act against it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. This is a document of the 23rd of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, it's a new document, 6056. May I apply to tender it, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P1708. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, around this time I want to show you another document which I believe is on the same day, it's Exhibit D30. It's at tab 577 of our list. Now, sir, this is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I believe this is a document that's supposed to be used in closed session, at least that's what e-court says on my screen, but I could always be wrong since I see the Registrar shaking his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Originally I remember when we tendered this document or when you tender a document there was a question mark as to whether these documents that we obtained last summer should be used in private session or not, but we have a confirmation that we can use them all in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, first if we go to -- well, looking at the header right here it says Republic of Serbian Krajina, Government of the Serbian District of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. Could we go to the last page, please. Yes. Well, the page before that, please. This is the stamp. In English. Right. Now, the document is issued here by at the time -- scroll down a little bit more, please, thank you very much, by at the time Prime Minister Goran Hadzic. First of all, have you had an occasion to review this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, Your Honours, because there's also a reply by Colonel Belic, I mean that the assistant commander for civil affairs of the pgmd or by then the 1st Mechanised Corps to the letter by Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. If we return to page 1, yes, if we scroll to the bottom of the page we see here that there is an introduction that the letter is written in the name of the Government of the Serbian District. We can now move to the next page and we see here that it's sent to the town commander of Ilok. Yes, can we zoom in the middle part of the document. Yes. Now, it deals here with discussions that have -- well, arise from problems between both sides. And there is a reference here to the fact that they are appointing the minister of justice, Mr. Vojin Susa, as a representative in relations with organs of the JNA, particularly in connection with the establishment of civilian authorities in the liberated areas of the Serbian district. Now, with respect to this part of the document, do you have any comments with the appointment of a minister to deal with the relations of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the comments would relate to the beginning of the document where Mr. Hadzic highlights apparent difficulties or problems in the co-operation -- I mean, identified by him in the co-operation of the relations between the JNA and the SAO SBWS civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And since it's addressed to Colonel Belic, it focuses on the area of Ilok.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. I'd like to put this document aside for a moment and go to 65 ter 6063, which is at tab 584. Now, the previous document, the letter we saw from Goran Hadzic, was on the 23rd of December. This one is the 29th of December, and as you can see on the bottom right-hand side it is signed, well, yes, by Vojin Susa for the government's commission. It is addressed here as: "Colonel, "Please be informed that the Government's Commission for organisation and conduct of the operation of moving in and temporary accommodation of the persons who fled from the area ... has convened a session to be held on 30 December 1991 at 1200 hours on the premises of the ... castle in Ilok ... "We believe that your presence would contribute to a better detection of problems," et cetera. Have you seen this document today -- when you were reviewing the new material?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen the document, Your Honours, and maybe I can provide some context or?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, when -- and this is -- what I wanted to say this is addressed in the report, but I addressed it in the new report that in October there is an agreement between the JNA and the Croatian authorities in Ilok, October 1991, concerning the -- what is described as the -- I call it the departure of Croatian civilians or the civilian population from Ilok by their own volition, which means that a large number of houses are empty in Ilok as a result. There was very little fighting in Ilok itself, so by the time of these documents, I mean for example 29 December 1991, efforts are undertaken to use these houses for Serbian refugees from other parts of Croatia, predominantly Western Slavonia because there many Serbs had to leave. And these -- based on -- again, on the other documents I have seen, there are some difficulties in how these Serbs from other parts of Croatia are allowed into these houses which were previously occupied by predominantly non-Serbs. The JNA highlights these problems, holds the local authorities accountable for certain shortcomings or difficulties that arise during that relocation process, including even also for the pressure or harassment against remaining non-Serbs in Ilok. And, okay, by the end of December 1991 a meeting is called by the representative of the local Serb authorities, inviting the JNA in order to discuss the matter and probably try to solve it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can I take you to page 2 of this document in both versions. So here we see a table, a list of residents of Vinkovci and Vukovar municipalities which is said to be drawn out according to the 1991 census. First of all, are you familiar with the 1991 census or the fact that it had been done, conducted?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, this is the census prior to the war, so I think it was a census at the level of the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And can I take you to page 14 in the English version, and we can stay in this format, actually, page 14, which is in B/C/S page 13. Thank you. We can scroll down a little bit in the English version. Yes. So here we see numbers broken down by what appears to be settlements, Tompojevci, Boksic, Tovarnik, and you have numbers indicating the population before the war and after the war. Have you seen documents of the kind in the material you've reviewed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. Among the documents that were available to me in September/October 2012, there was quite a substantial number of documents, JNA documents, which provide information on the ethnic distribution or the ethnic composition of the population after the war in 1991. So they -- the JNA units in Eastern Slavonia regularly compile reports on the then-ethnic compositions in the various areas in their zones of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if we move to the next page very briefly for both versions. Here we see other villages and the same type of information, the numbers before the war and after the war. And is it correct that the following pages which succeed also have a number of other villages in this bundle?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We can keep moving on but --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents were very comprehensive. I mean, they addressed each village and municipalities, and then the villages -- I mean, the municipalities, the towns, and the villages in the zones of responsibility of the various JNA units in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, might I tender this document which is 65 ter 6063?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document shall be assigned Exhibit P1709. And just for the record, the first page of this document has already been admitted as D28. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, could we display 65 ter 6065 which is at tab 586. So this is another one of the new documents. Do you see on the screen, Mr. Theunens, that this is issued by the 1st Proletarian Guards Mechanised Division on the 31st of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And here it says: "Report on the government session." And it is sent to the 1st Military District. In the first paragraph we see that at a meeting of the government commission for population and temporary accommodation has been held on the 30th of December, 1991, at 1200 hours in a castle in Ilok, organised by the Serbian District of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. So does this relate to the document we just saw before that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, it relates to the invitations sent by Mr. Susa to the Colonel Belic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So in the second paragraph here we see the individuals who have attended. On behalf of the Serbian district you have the Deputy Prime Minister Bogunovic; you have the minister of justice, Susa; a member of the Executive Council; and on behalf of the JNA you have Colonels Miljkovic and Milan Belic. I want to take you to page 2 and in the B/C/S we can still remain on page 1 and move towards the bottom. So at the top of the page here you see that it is said that Bogunovic will deal with the coming task to set up accurate records of temporarily populated persons. Perhaps we should look at the translation here because it says "temporarily populated persons," I'm not sure if that's the term that's used in the B/C/S, but I will ask for a revision. At the bottom of the page you see a paragraph which begins with "deputy prime minister," so we saw on the first page this was Bogunovic. "Deputy Prime Minister said: 'We do not know what our goals are ... we want the structure here to change ... some people do not understand military administration well.'" And this is followed by a comment by the 1st pgmd officer who said: "These quotes illustrate that the government wants to change the structure of the population at all costs ..." I'll stop there. What is your comment with respect to the assessment of the JNA here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this comment is consistent with the observations made in other JNA documents at that time as well as with observations made by the Secretary-General of the United Nations at a much later stage, but in the reports on the implementation of the United Nations Security Council Resolutions concerning UNPROFOR which include also evaluations of the degree of implementation of the Vance Plan and analysis of the situation in the UNPAs, regular reference is made to efforts involving, for example, the structure we discussed earlier, the PJM, so the milicija, in pressure or harassment of members of minority or non-Serbs that is still remaining in the UNPAs, and this is not confined to 1992 but also the later years.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And -- now, from the JNA's perspective, Mr. Theunens, what measures are available to the town commanders and to the 1st Military District when they're aware of the situation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the documents I have reviewed, Your Honours, the first -- I mean, it's not really a measure, but the thing they do is to report to their superiors, and this goes -- for example, in this case it goes all the way up the 1st Military District, as well as addressing it in the situation with their counterparts in among the authorities of the SAO SBWS. I don't recall at this stage any other measures that are undertaken by members of the JNA when they come across situations or activities as they are highlighted here in relation to pressure on non-Serbs, even if there are, indeed, orders through the chain of command to prevent such pressure, but I haven't seen anything or I don't recall seeing anything indicating what specific measures are undertaken to implement those orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I apply to tender this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1710.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very briefly on this topic, could we look at 65 ter 6121 which is at tab 619. Thank you. Now, we see that this is a document from the 1st Mechanised Brigade command. It is being sent to the 1st Mechanised Corps to the organs for civilian affairs. It states here that: "Further to your memo ... of the 7th of March ... we enclose details of the ethnic structure of the population in our zone of responsibility ..." And: "We ... draw your attention to the fact that the numbers change every day due to the movement of the population." Can we move to the next page in both versions, please. Now, we see a document which is in content similar to what we've seen before but perhaps in format slightly different or we see the population before and after. First of all, do you see in relation to the municipality of Vukovar, the first block of numbers here we see, you have numbers, Croats, Serbs, Ukrainians, et cetera, which are - how would I say? - generally referred to in the thousands, all numbers end with zeros here. Would you have a comment in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could think that that is a general estimate, but in the -- a census was conducted before the war with -- whereby -- I mean, there were detailed figures available or detailed data available as to the ethnic composition of the SFRY. I'm not in a position to explain why these accurate numbers apparently do not seem to be reflected in these statistics, unless other boundaries are being used for municipalities, the municipalities -- for the towns and villages that make up the municipality of Vukovar, but again it's more for a demographer I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, and if you look at the numbers below that -- now we see numbers that are bit more specific. Now, how would the JNA have reached these figures?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the documents I reviewed do not describe the methodology that was used by the JNA. I mean, they could have made an account by going house by house or they could have relied on data from local authorities or whatever records, so I cannot give you a precise answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: May I tender this document, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1711. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, on this very topic we have two or three other documents which have again same structure, cover page with a table attached to it. If there are no objections, and this was in the e-mail that I sent to the Defence last week, I would like to tender the following three documents which are 65 ters 6127, 6124, and 6158. Again, if there is an objection I could display them on the screen, but we say that they have the same format.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You have been able to look at them, Mr. Gosnell?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: They shall be assigned exhibit numbers P1712, P1713, and P1714 in a chronological order. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: May I ask you, Mr. Theunens, to look at another document which is 65 ter 6102 at tab 608. Thank you. This is a document of the 1st Mechanised Corps, this time of the 22nd of February, 1992. We see here the town Principovac and to be delivered to the 1st Military District. Here -- the report relates to a meeting which was held in the municipality of Mirkovci on the 21st of February, 1991, which was attended by local organs, police station commanders. And if we move to the next page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian, you say 20 -- 1991? Wasn't it 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's my mistake. It is 1992. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And we see also on this page that police station commanders, commanders of the TO attended the meeting. Towards the middle of that page we see that the meeting was led by the corps commander, Major-General Mico Delic. And the course of the meeting followed the agenda and pressing problems were discussed. Now, I'd like to take you to page 2 -- well, page 3, sorry, in the English version, item 5. In the B/C/S it should be bottom of page 1, I believe. Yes. Now, at the end of this meeting it appears that there is a general assessment which was made, and the civilian affairs organ proposed the following: "For measures to be taken at the level of the government of Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem, and Baranja ... to quickly resolve the issue of settlement in areas that were hitherto unsettled ...," and we see five villages here, "... and to more effectively change the national make-up in places already settled." Now, we saw an earlier document where the JNA was commenting on the fact that the government seems to be pressing the matter on changing the ethnic structure. What do you make out of this proposal here in this JNA document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- I mean, this paragraph shows -- in this document shows that the civilian authorities still have the lead, but that contrary to previous documents here the representatives of the JNA appear to concur with changing the national make-up or the ethnic composition of the location and -- which is different from other JNA documents I have seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you see under item number (b) that the JNA proposes here: "For all displaced persons, regardless of their nationality, who have participated in Ustasha units on any basis whatsoever to be prohibited from returning to this area." Now, have you seen any other documents which deals with the issue of the returning of the population?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously I have, but I mean it's a bit of a general question. The issue of non-Serbs and their relations with what is described as Ustashas is raised in several documents. I mean, in some documents by the JNA it is questioned whether they can still stay, and in these documents you see that it's both questioned or they can be questioned by the JNA as well as there are JNA documents reflecting questions by the local Serb authorities on the right, between brackets, to remain for non-Serbs who are suspected of having maintained relations with what was described as Ustasha authorities. Some of the documents talk about the need to protect loyal members, I mean "loyal" members of minorities of non-Serbs, and again these are both documents from the JNA as well as -- or documents where the JNA expresses its views as well as documents where the JNA reflects the views of members of the SAO SBWS authorities. So it's a complex matter. I think also for this document, in addition to this paragraph as well as the previous one on change the ethnic make-up, it dates from the 22nd of February, whereas in earlier documents, as I said, the JNA seems to be denouncing what they consider efforts by the local civilian authorities SAO SBWS authorities to change the ethnic make-up. So the matter is quite complex and I think it's important to look at the documents in context.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I tender this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1715. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So it is time for the break. Just in terms of management I will have probably another 20 minutes after the break and I should be finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Theunens, second break. We'll come back at 12.45. Thank you very much. [The witness stands down].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, with respect to the pending translation which is MFI 1692, Exhibit 1692, we are expecting to receive it during the course of the day. So I just wanted to update you on that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I have a few more documents to show you before I complete my examination. I would like you to look at 65 ter 6145 which is at tab 632. Thank you. Now, this is a document of the 1st Mechanised Corps on the 19th of March which is being sent to the 1st Military District. It is a daily report of the organs of civilian affairs. There is a description of the situation again here in the first page. I'd like you to go to page 2 in the English version first, please, and, yes, the next version and look at item number 6. Now, again with respect to the topic we were dealing with earlier before the break, if you read the first sentence here it -- it states here that: "The moving out of the local population is being organised by the local civilian authorities, with supervision and security provided by the IS, expansion unknown, of the Government of the Serbian district ... the person in charge is Ziko Vevcevic." Now, first of all, have you had an opportunity to review this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a hundred per cent sure because, I mean, at this stage I don't know what IS stands for, so I could check during the break in the lexicon or something, but at this stage I don't -- so I'm not a hundred per cent sure I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. I have another document which may clarify the issue. Now, on the issue of the moving out of the local population under the supervision of the Serbian district, do you have any views on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Objection, this is outside of the scope of the report as far as I know unless there is a reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This is the same topic that we've been dealing with for the past hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, now I'm objecting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, if there is no solid basis for an objection, Your Honours, I would propose to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, the basis of the objection is that it's outside of the scope of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the report deals with the issue of town commands, of the local commands that were created by the JNA and the matters that they have been reporting. The issues of resettlement is included in the report. From the top of my head I can remember the Helsinki Watch Report which makes a very clear reference to the issue of resettlement and these are matters that are in the report. These are new documents obviously which we obtained last summer and which expand on the topic. I don't see any difference between this topic and the ones that we've been looking at for the past -- today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: To my knowledge, Mr. President, there is no section or paragraph of the report that attributes responsibility for moving out of civilian populations in this area to the district government of the SBWS and that's now the subject that we're embarking -- well, continuing upon and we object on the basis that it's outside of the scope of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian, the Trial Chamber is of the opinion that you should move on to another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Your Honours, I apologise for -- I know you've already ruled, but at page 123, again, if I can come back to this part of the report, we're looking at the implementation of the justice system and here you have a 21 January 1992 Helsinki Watch report which is quoted by Mr. Theunens which are being sent to both civilian and military authorities. You have Milosevic was copied on it, Blagoje Adzic was copied on it. And the second paragraph that is quoted here there is a reference to abuses and indiscriminate and disproportionate use of force against civilian targets, disappearances, forced displacement, resettlement of civilian populations. This is a topic that is being dealt with in the report. Now, another issue here is these documents have been on the list since the month of January. This document has been listed since then. This is the first we hear that there's an objection to dealing with the issue of forcible displacement being connected to the local government. This is an issue that was also dealt with with our MUP expert. So it comes to me as a complete surprise that now at this 11th hour we're being told we cannot use documents related to the civilian authorities and forcible displacement and this is what we've been dealing with for the past hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian, I don't think that the fact that we are dealing with this for the past hour prevents the Defence, if they have good cause, to say this is as far as we will go and now we object.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I understand that part. Maybe that comment was not necessary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: -- but coming back to the issue that I was ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, the matter seems to be here in the report, page 123.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, what we have here is an extract from a Helsinki Watch report dated the 21st of January, 1992, and as I understand the Prosecution's argument they're saying that any subject matter that's mentioned in a document that happens to be cited in the report then provides an adequate nexus to discuss all manner of documents. I would just ask this question: What subject would not be encompassed within the breadth of this Helsinki Watch report? I can't think of anything. And surely the purpose of Rule 94 ter is that we have reasonable notice of extremely complicated matters and opinions that are going to be presented by an expert. And to allow this as a bridgehead to introduce all manner of documents for comment by the expert I would suggest is not appropriate. And just one final matter, if I may say, Mr. President, it's also a question of the scope of the expertise. Dr. Nielsen, of course, had a different expertise than does Mr. Theunens, and we did hear a considerable commentary from Dr. Nielsen, but as I say Dr. Nielsen had a different expertise than Mr. Theunens. So we do maintain the objection and there is a distinction between Mr. Theunens and Dr. Nielsen. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Request for reconsideration overruled or denied, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. I will move on, Your Honours, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now -- just a moment, please. Now, the document that we looked at before the break, Mr. Theunens, if you'll remember was the one which dealt with a report of the civilian affairs of the 22nd of February, and there there were some proposals made by the civilian organs affairs if you remember, some proposals for measures to be taken. I would like you to look at 65 ter 6150 at tab 364, please. Now, this is a document of the 23rd of March, 1992. You see that it is a conclusion the Republic of Serbian Krajina Ministry of Internal Affairs is required to immediately start sorting out the state of security in the Serbian region in co-operation with the 1st Military District. Now, first of all, with respect to the terminology here, "in co-operation," does that, again, match with instructions 588-1 and 588-3 we saw earlier?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, it confirms -- it's consistent with what I mentioned earlier; that is, not only the consistency with 588-1 and 588-3 but also the 1st Military District order 2436-1 of the 20th of November, 1991, that is that the JNA assists the organs of the SAO SBWS authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And the explanation provided below here is that: "Due to the poor or non-existent protection of property and persons ... the Serbian Region government has decided as stated above." Now, with respect to measures which was related to the previous document which was admitted, have you seen any other types of decisions of the kind?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm objecting if the question encompasses documents that are not issued by a military organ.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You're not answering yet Mr. Demirdjian's question, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but I mean -- I don't know whether it's relevant, but also the previous point raised by the Defence, I have quoted, for example, passages from reports by the UN Secretary-General on the implementation of the relevant Resolutions concerning UNPROFOR and we discussed that earlier where the PJM is discussed. And, you know, if you look at footnote 1159, mention is made by -- I mean, I will read it out from the report on page 383: "These paramilitary units," and this is referring to the PJM, "engage in acts of terrorism against minorities especially in Sector East and to a lesser extent Sector South and appear to enjoy complete impunity." It is correct that I have not analysed the human rights situation in SBWS in detail because that is indeed outside the scope of my report, but I have on the basis of the material that I could consult analysed the activities of the armed structures. We have highlighted the JNA, SFRY armed forces, the TO, local Serb TO, paramilitaries and volunteers, as well as the armed structures -- I mean as well as the MUP, sorry, and including -- in SBWS and their relation with the civilian authorities and their activities. So coming back to this document, yeah, it's in line and even the previous document I would say is in line with the material I was reviewing and which I have addressed in the report, the only distinction being that I didn't have those documents available prior to the dead-line that was imposed by the Trial Chamber, so therefore it was physically impossible for me to review them within the set dead-line.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may respond to the objection. The nature of the document is what Mr. Gosnell is objecting to. I believe that the military expert is allowed to use all sources that are available to him, not only military documents. And I believe you have seen already in the report that numerous gazettes and other documents issued by civilian organs are also used by the military expert, so I believe that there is no grounds for this objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That last objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if I were to -- yes, my question was with respect to the measures related to the -- this document that we have seen, have you seen any other types of decisions of this kind?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And with respect to the military, have you seen any documents which call for measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Objection. I think that that question was asked and answered, unless I misunderstood the previous question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Well, let's have the clarification then, whether the witness in the previous answer referred to military documents as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. The first question was broad in the sense that I think it covered all categories --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you -- with your objection, Mr. Gosnell, I had the impression that we narrowed the scope of and the kind of documents we were talking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Except, Mr. President, that you overruled my objection and the question was posed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I know. But still it can -- it can direct the witness's attention in a certain direction. So just let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- let's ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I understand. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, my answer to the first question in context in relation to this document by Mr. Demirdjian was that I haven't seen any documents issued by the SAO SBWS concerning the kind of measures that should be taken. And as I mentioned earlier this morning, I have seen several military documents from the SSNO and the 1st Military District as well as of subordinate units which we have discussed over the previous days, whereby they call for preventing harassment of minorities and criminal behaviour, but I don't remember seeing any document specifying the kind of measures that should be taken in order to implement these calls to prevent harassment or either criminal behaviour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, with that topic in mind, would you please look at --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, before I move on, may I tender this document, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1716. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And could I ask you to look at 65 ter 6099, please, which is at tab 606. So here we have another document that the 1st Mechanised Corps from the 18th of February, 1992, and looking here at page 1, it refers here to a warning from the 1st Military District that a large number of complaints by citizens have been received recently and these complaints concerned the inappropriate action by local TO commanders, presidents of local commune, and other authorities. Now, here he recalls that despite his, I suspect he means the 1st Military District command, and our express orders to desist from driving out non-Serbs using violent means -- we'll have to turn to page 2 to see the end of that sentence, these instances have not only not been prevented but have become even more frequent and cruel. Then this is followed by an order. If you look at the bottom of this page, the 1st Mechanised Corps commander is appointing a commission to deal with these complaints. Now, you see then the first name here, Colonel Novica Gusic, we have seen his name in other documents; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think he was the commander at that stage of the 1st Mechanised Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And -- sorry, this document is being issued by the 1st Mechanised Corps, and if we go to page 4 --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I mean, I use my cheat sheet, but I summarise some of the documents. He was the assistant commander for civil affairs --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the -- I mean, this is visible through other documents, of the 1st Mechanised Corps which succeeded to the 1st Proletarian Guards Mechanised Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. And here we see the document is signed by Major-General Delic --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, Mico Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If we return to page 3 we see the rest of the names of the members of this commission. And under item 4 we see the term: "Loyal non-Serbian citizens are to be protected from threats of liquidation and from pressures of all sorts ..." Now, are you aware of what he is referring to here by using the term "loyal non-Serbian citizens"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, seen in the context of other documents, these are citizens of non-Serbian ethnicity who did not join Croatian units or forces when the conflict erupted between on one hand Croatian side and on the other hand the Serbian side in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And then we see at the bottom of the page another order to prevent paramilitary units from being organised, et cetera. So does this tie-in with the answer you provided earlier with respect to having seen documents where measures are taken by military units?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, when I talk about measures, it is more like punitive measures, i.e., were people arrested, were being investigated, were people punished one way or the other. When I said that I haven't seen any documents concerning concrete measures, it's I haven't seen any documents from the SSNO or the 1st Military District or subordinate units concerning, for example, investigation of alleged crimes or alleged harassment or organs by security -- reports by security organs from after December 1991, whereby they investigate specific cases in detail. I mean, the reports I have seen talk about general behaviour and, for example, I mean there are still security organ reports on the activities of Arkan and his group, but it's quite general without really investigating specific cases. So that's what I meant on my previous answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: May I tender this document, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P1717. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm mindful of the time, Your Honours. I will have two more documents before I complete. May I call up 65 ter 6179 which is at tab 654. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This is a document again from one of the town commands being sent to the 1st Mechanised Corps in Principovac, and it's a submission of an Official Note which relates to a meeting held between the town command of Ilok with representatives of the UNPROFOR. Mr. Theunens, have you had the opportunity to review this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, by the 21st of April what was the situation with respect to the UNPROFOR forces in the region?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as -- and this is also clear from the document, as far as the territory covered by the SAO SBWS or at that time in UN parlance Sector East there was already -- there was a presence of UNPROFOR in the area, both military and civilian. I cannot say whether the full deployment of the peacekeeping forces had been achieved by then in Sector East but at least there was some presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, we see in the second paragraph that UNPROFOR is spelling out the importance of establishing co-operation with the civilian organs and the JNA. And under item 3 we see here that there is a discussion about focus to be turned to the question of forced eviction which according to the UNPROFOR representative is the most acute problem in this area. Now, again, is this consistent with the other documentation you have seen?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And with respect to the UNPROFOR's assessment here, and this is April of 1992, I think you may have answered this partially before, but how does the situation develop during the course of 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in my previous answer to Your Honours I mentioned a -- I quoted from a report on the implementation of Security Council Resolution 743 and 762, I mean this is on page 383 of the amalgamated report. This is report from September 1992, and according to that report including in Sector East the PJM, so the special police units, are involved in -- I mean "in acts of terrorism against minorities."

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I offer this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1718. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, with respect to this collection of documents we had sent an e-mail to the Defence last week. Again, I'm mindful of the time so I will not take court time to deal with it, but we may deal with this in our written submission next week. Mainly the issue is that there are several documents relating to the same topics, abandoned properties, resettlement, and the relationship between the civilian organs and the JNA. Of course it is not humanely possible to deal with all of them in the course of this examination, but we will make a submission with respect to that with our filing which you ordered us to file a week after the completion of the testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, we will not look at the other sections of your report, but it is correct that you have a section dealing with the relations between the SVK and the Yugoslav Army and this is from pages 298 onwards of your report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, as I say, I'm not going to delve into that. There is also a section at page 307 onwards where you deal with the relation between the SVK and the VRS?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours. It starts at the bottom of 307.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And again, considering the time, I'm not going to go into the details here. You've described it in your report. I would like us to quickly look at page 310 of your report. If we could display that on the screen, and the B/C/S page number is 357. Yes. Now, here you're dealing with the issue of the Posavina corridor and we see a map here. First of all, is this your own annotation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, it's a map I drew myself just to visualise the location of the area known as the Posavina corridor, which basically -- I mean, Posavina means the valley of the Sava, the Sava being located -- I mean, coinciding with the border -- being the border between Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And with respect to that you deal with the orders that were sent by or dispatched by Milan Martic with respect to the use of the RSK MUP in this conflict. And I would like you to take a look at 65 ter 1159 which is at tab 672. Now, in your report at pages 310 and 311 you deal with a number of orders issued during the month of June of 1992. Here we have the minutes of the government of the RSK which were held in Knin on the 9th of June, 1992. You see the individuals who are attending this session, which include Zdravko Zecevic, who is the prime minister at the time, and Milan Martic himself. I'd like to take you to the top of page 5 in the English version, and that would be page 2 in the B/C/S version. Do you see the first sentence here: "Minister ... Martic spoke about the problems which have arisen following the closing of the corridor towards Serbia. After a debate the government authorised the MUP to do all it could to open the corridor." Now, with respect to this, can you -- do you have any comments with respect to the fact that Milan Martic addresses the government about this issue?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's an -- I mean, as I mentioned in the report on page 309 I quote from an article in Vojska Krajina, which was the official magazine of the SVK, where Milan Martic explains the importance of the corridor, as it is the only physical or land connection between Serbia, the territory controlled by Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the RSK. And since, as is mentioned in document, the corridor is closed there is -- this can create serious problems. And so we know that by that time the Bosnian Serbs conduct operations there. Also can highlight - and it's mentioned in the report - that the corridor -- opening a corridor, establishing a corridor between Semberija, i.e., the north-eastern part of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Krajina, so the western part of Bosnia-Herzegovina is one of the six strategic goals. So all of this highlights the importance of unrestricted access for the Serbs meeting in the RSK or in the SR BiH and subsequently the RS to this corridor and Martic wants to alert the government to the importance of reopening the corridor and contributing to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That is the only question I have for this document, Your Honours. May I seek to tender this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1719. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. This concludes the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens, for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, with respect to the report, it is at 65 ter 5988 which we seek to tender at this moment, and we have also two errata sheets. One of them is based on the amalgamated report. It is at 65 ter 6416. And we have a second errata sheet, an additional one which was prepared while Mr. Theunens was proofed here, and it's 6416.1, so we seek to tender these three documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, we would take the same position as we did in respect of Dr. Nielsen's report, namely that the admission of the report should be deferred until -- at the very least until the end of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Any objection to that, Mr. Demirdjian?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'm in your hands, Your Honours, on this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We'll wait then. Cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Your English is impeccable and you clearly have a mastery of military terminology, but sometimes it's helpful just to clarify some basic definitions to avoid confusion later on. And I just wanted to start with a couple of definitions, if I may. Would you agree with me that if person A is inspecting a unit or an organisation, that that is a function or could be indicative of command and control or at the very least authority?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would seek clarification of the question because -- I mean I have included the definition of inspection as a function of command and control as it exists in the SFRY armed forces, and there -- since it is -- can be -- or since it is a function of command and control, it can indicate command and control. However, on the other side it can be reported, for example, in a press report that a visiting authority is inspecting another detachment whereby in fact there is no relation, no command and control relation between that visiting authority on the one hand and the other detachment on the other hand. So I think I would be careful in answering the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So it depends on the context?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the specific situation. I mean, if you ask me as I said inspection is a function of command and control, obviously the one who has command and control can or has to inspect. But if the word "inspection" would be used in a non-purely military context, I would have to look at the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can you at least accept that it's indicative of authority?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not necessarily authority in relation to the unit that is being inspected. I mean, given the example I gave of -- I mean the minister of foreign affairs of Serbia -- no, that's not a good example, but the minister of foreign affairs of Belgium can visit the Netherlands and there will be an honour guard maybe at the airport if he comes by airplane and he may inspect the honour guard, but that's where it ends. It doesn't mean that the minister of foreign affairs of Belgium has any command over elements of the Dutch armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if person A says that he is going to hold accountable person B or unit B, would you say that that's indicative of authority of person A over that unit?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean if it's put in a military document and signed by obviously the commander of that unit, then yes. But again, I would -- I prefer to look at specific documents and then draw conclusions from that instead of giving general answers which could be misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you consider yourself a part of the Prosecution team?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because -- I mean, for sure not now -- I mean not since the last four years because I've been very busy doing other things. But even when I was -- the time-period I was at the ICTY, it is correct that I did some work in relation to the Prosecution activities -- Prosecution activities concerning Mr. Goran Hadzic, but that was initially and it was part of my work on the Milosevic case. And it is also obvious that when I was working as a military analyst supporting the Prosecution team in the Vukovar 3 trial, if I can call it like that, that I came across material that is also relevant in the context of this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: While you were employed by the office of the -- by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, did you consider yourself to be part of the various Prosecution teams to which you were providing some form of service, let's say?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're very polite because I've heard other Defence lawyers asking or trying to make this kind of or addressing this point in a much more direct or even I would say less courteous way. I was obviously member of a team, but I think as -- and you are familiar with my -- with the methodology I applied. As I have mentioned also in answer to such questions in other trials, applying the methodology refers to reviewing the material. It is -- I would -- I mean a professional analyst, irrespective of which "side" he or she is "working" for, a professional analyst should not be influenced by that aspect. I mean, I was free to review the material that was available at the OTP. It may well have been that the Office of the Prosecutor asked me to look at additional material, but again whether I was in the Office of the Prosecutor or in any other situation here, the conclusions I draw from that material are not depending of the side or the team or the whatever I was part of. It is -- the conclusions are based on my understanding and my analysis of these documents or other information material.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That was a very long answer, Mr. Theunens, and I'm not sure that you finally came to the point. The question was: Do you consider -- did you consider yourself a part of the various Prosecution teams with whom you interacted?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would say from a human point of view I hoped that I was member of a team, but what I tried to clarify is that the services, as you call it, that I was providing to these teams, for me it doesn't matter whether they call themselves Prosecution or whatever. The -- I was autonomous in doing the analysis I did, and this is the result of my work.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You participated in meetings with Prosecutors; correct? I think that could be a yes or no answer?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And did you discuss strategy in those meetings, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it really depends of each team I think -- I didn't keep the count of all the cases I worked on, but especially -- for sure in the Milosevic case issues like strategy were being discussed, yes. And maybe also in the Vukovar 3 team, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you provide strategy information or advice to the -- whoever was working on the Hadzic case?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to remember because, as I said, initially I have -- I believe I was involved -- I arrived in 2001 and as part of my work on Milosevic was in 2002 or 2003, I believe there was some kind of a Hadzic team or at least some information was collected on -- in relation to that case. But after that, I'm not familiar with the existence of a Hadzic team during the time I was here in The Hague. So I left in April 2009.
