When I came back - and I mentioned that I think in answer to one of the first questions - I think it was in April 2012 but I can check it in my cheat sheets, I had contact with the Hadzic Prosecution team and I told them, yes, I would need these and these type of documents in order to write a report on the underlying issues. And on the basis of that, a request was drafted and sent to the authorities of the Republic of Serbia, and these are the so-called new documents which I consider very helpful for the kind of tasking I had received.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let's go back to an earlier time. Did you assist in drafting the indictment or did you review a draft of the indictment before it was issued?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no specific recollection for the Hadzic case, but for other cases indeed I was involved not so much in drafting an indictment but in reviewing it for the -- for aspects like the correct use of military terminology, some historical aspects, but for sure - I mean just to clarify, I was never involved, I'm not a lawyer, in kind of building legal theories or prosecutional theories because that's not my expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: In the Seselj case you testified at page 4045, and that's 1D296, Defence tab 368, but we don't need to bring it up: "Like any other team member, I could participate in meetings where, for example, the issue of witnesses to be called was discussed, and my contribution then mainly consisted in providing a factual background, whereas to the position or the knowledge of the witness." So is that right that you participated in meetings and assisted in choosing witnesses?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I -- sorry. I expressed occasional views on witnesses, again based on my military expertise. When a military witness is being discussed, I could help maybe with CV information or clarify the duties of that person to people with less military background in the Prosecution team.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you were involved in interviewing witnesses; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. I was involved in interviewing military witnesses, mainly I mean JNA members or members of the TO.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please pause between answer and question, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You were involved in proofing sessions --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I apologise for the transcription.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you were involved in proofing sessions immediately before witnesses testified; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. I mean, I'm giving general answers. I cannot say -- I wish to clarify, it's not in every case -- like in the Hadzic case, you know, I mean, this is my -- except for the two meetings I had or maybe three meetings with the Prosecution in relation to my report, I have not done -- I haven't provided any contribution or I didn't have any involvement in the work of the Prosecution team.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Between 2001 and 2009, who was your supervisor or supervisors?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My first supervisor was Mr. Peter Nicholson who was the team leader of the military analysis team. At one moment in time, I'm not sure anymore whether it was in 2005 or 2004 he left for the ICC, and then Mr. Ewan Brown took over as supervisor or leader of the military analysis team in the Office of the Prosecutor. He also left for the ICC. And then a Mr. Phil Coo took over as team leader of the military analysis team and these are all military analysts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And when was that that he took over as head of the team?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall exactly. I think between 2006 and 2008 I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So did he supervise you from, at the very least, 2007, 2008, and 2009?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but with the caveat that I believe that in 2009 he had left -- I think he left in the course of 2008 and there was at that time no direct supervisor, and then it was solved by having Mr. Bob Reid as the supervisor in the latter part of 2008 and also the first half of 2009 when I was still here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Was there any discussion as to whether it was appropriate for you to be supervised by someone whom the Milutinovic Trial Chamber determined was not sufficiently independent to be treated as an expert, as was the case with Mr. Coo?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar, Your Honours, with the decisions of the Trial Chamber in relation to Mr. Coo, but I don't recall that that issue was of any relevance -- not of any relevance, but that issue also arose when discussing the supervision of the military analysis team. I don't recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let me put it this way: Did you yourself engage in any soul-searching about whether you had sufficient independence to be considered an expert after that decision was rendered?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, for me there are two issues in this question. I will start with the easiest one. The issue of an expert is not up to me to decide; that's up to the Trial Chamber. And the first issue whether I have sufficient independence, I think I've answered that. I think I've always -- I mean, in all the time since I worked even as a platoon commander in the military and until now, I always had the privilege whenever I did analysis that I could draw my analysis in an independent manner or in the case that it is now I consulted with my team members. My supervisors may have different views, but I -- and I may enter into a discussion with them, but they will not change my analysis or the analysis of my team, but we are -- that's our job, we apply the methodology, and this is it. And especially at the ICTY. I have no -- I think I testified about that in previous trials. I may have had different views or views that differed from those of the Prosecution team in relation to certain issues, be it witnesses or be it their how certain facts were addressed. And okay, it's -- I would say it's the call of the senior trial attorney at the end of the day. But from a methodological point of view, I have always tried to consciously apply my methodology on the material that was in front of me and that I had the privilege to review without being influenced by outside factors. And if you want, I can address the issue of bias in further detail and how this is addressed in the methodology, but maybe that is for another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do your reports transparently reflect what you just told us; namely, that there are occasions when you have disagreements with the position of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, my reports are not about the nature of my relations with the Office of the Prosecutor or whether -- but my reports are analysis of documentation within the scope of a general task that has been given to me by the Office of the Prosecutor. But it -- as I said, analysing or -- yeah, analysing relations and the nature of relations with the Office of the Prosecutor is not part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: There's an expression that we see frequently in the documents as well as in your report and that is "zone of responsibility." I wasn't able to see a definition in your report of that concept. Could you help us and define that term, please?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Perhaps without on this occasion consulting your report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No -- I mean, the reason I want to consult the report is to show you where it should have been included because, for example, it is included in the 1983 regulations on the light infantry brigade. I use "zone of responsibility" because I couldn't find "area of responsibility," but it's basically the area or the zone where a unit is operating and where it is responsible for the operations that it is conducting there and where - and now I'm paraphrasing a definition but I think it's important to highlight - where the commander of the unit, given the three principles of command and control, is responsible for all activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And to your mind, is the concept of a zone of responsibility purely a geographic or territorial -- in other words, a spatial concept, or do you think that there is something else that defines it, something in addition to that? In other words, let me break this down into a very simple example. And of course as you know, sir, this is very germane of the issues we're discussing here. But if a unit enters into the zone of responsibility - when I say "a unit," let me rephrase that - a group of soldiers enter into a zone of responsibility and they have no prior affiliation and they're armed and they take up arms on behalf of one side to the conflict, is it correct that it's the duty of the commander in that zone of operations to subordinate them?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, just to clarify, I assume you're talking about friendly soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's correct, and that's a word you used the other day and I appreciated your use of that word, yes, friendly forces.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. It is the duty -- and again, I mean this is also specified in JNA documents, to subordinate them or to remove them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You're very categorical in that answer. Are there any limitations on that in your view?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am categorical because I was thinking of a number of documents I have seen. For example, we have discussed those documents in relation to paramilitaries and volunteers, where it is -- it is stated that they have to be subordinated to the JNA or they should be removed. Now, if the limitations, then I would prefer to see specific documents because otherwise it's abstract.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And your view is that they would be -- that this obligation of the commander in that zone of responsibility, that arises as a matter of law and doctrine or both?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we keep -- if we take in mind an example we discussed, namely, the presidential order number 73 of the 10th of December, then it's not just a matter of doctrine but also a matter of law. 10th of December -- sorry, 10th of December, 1991, just to be accurate in the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You're not saying, are you, that this obligation arises only on the 10th of December, 1991, are you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying that. But that -- this is the clearest example I see from the law. But otherwise if you show me an article. And I can also verify the Law on Defence if you want during the breaks I have in order to assist you better.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, there are quite a few articles and quite a few laws and regulations, but you're well familiar with this subject matter and the proposition I'm putting to you is simply this: Would it have been understood by JNA commanders in an area or a zone of responsibility, notwithstanding any specific reaffirmations of that responsibility, that it's their obligation because units entering into their zone of responsibility are by law, doctrine, regulations, subordinate to them that they must take measures to either bring them under control, discipline them, or eject them from the zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, from a purely theoretical point of view, and I mean by that my review of the legislation and the doctrine, I would agree a hundred per cent with you. However, and this is where I think it becomes important to look at all the documents, reviewing military documentation - and we have discussed the categories before - apply -- I mean, there is a documentation in relation to the operations in Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, and Western Srem. There we see that it's for various reasons quite difficult to implement -- [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm doing it again. Now I know what I'm doing wrong. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, to -- it's quite difficult to implement or enforce this I would say basic rule, and this explains for example why, and we have seen these documents, the commander of the 1st Military District reportedly issues orders and instructions to his subordinate commanders to maintain military control and to subordinate local forces and so on. Just to finish, another complicating factor is the fact that we see units that were not foreseen by doctrine, i.e., party-affiliated paramilitary/volunteer units/TO, as well as local Serb TO, they were not foreseen in doctrine, so it appears that some of the subordinate commanders are -- yeah, are confused --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If I can just stop you there, if I may, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Gosnell please make a pause between -- Mr. Gosnell, please make a pause between question and answer. We have to catch up with you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I sincerely apologise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's difficult, of course, if you want to interrupt the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's the last thing I wish to do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But, if, I mean, if you allow me just to finish the sentence that it appears that some subordinate commanders I wouldn't say are confused, but there's no uniformity in handling the issue and I think the example of the commander of the 12th Novi Sad Corps, General Andrija Biorcevic, and I've spoken a few times about the video, but the video is very clear on that. He sees Arkan, actually, as an important -- Arkan and his group as an important element of his forces, whereas at the same time you see documents from the 1st Military District, from security organs, highlighting the alleged involvement of Arkan in crimes and other -- I mean not only against civilians but also against the JNA. So there is a bit of a contradiction indicating that there is some degree of confusion as to which attitude to adopt towards volunteer/paramilitary units as well as local Serb TO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That was a very long sentence to finish, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I promise that we're going to come to the Biorcevic statement and many other particularities, but right now I just want to get some parameters set with you, if I could. And I entirely understand the distinction you're making between on the one hand individual volunteers popping up in a zone of responsibility which does appear to be contemplated, as I believe your report indicates, by the Law on All People's Defence. But as you point out in your report, there is no specific authorisation for a unit as such to show up in the zone of responsibility. But notwithstanding that distinction and notwithstanding whatever illegality may be being carried out by those people, you'd agree it doesn't affect the zone commander's obligation; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you'd also agree, I think, that if that group or those individuals, separately or individually, are engaging in acts of indiscipline, it's not permissible for the commander in the zone of responsibility to say: Well, I'm just washing my hands of you, correct, if they're friendly forces?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's easier for me to look at specific documents, but in general terms I would agree with you, claiming that they're not under your responsibility is not an excuse in a sense that given, again, the orders that I have -- I mean given the doctrine and the orders I have mentioned, the commander has to use his power and his means either -- I mean to subordinate them or to remove them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And where is the contour, the boundary line, between an individual who arrives, takes up arms, fights as a friendly force along with the JNA, and then commits a petty crime, stealing a loaf of bread? Is that something that it's the obligation of the zone commander to punish in accordance with the subordination or would you say that that does not extend to the obligation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The petty crime would fall -- I refer to the military discipline, the military justice system, as well as earlier provisions -- the provisions we have discussed earlier, that is, that -- I mean starting with the law, anyone who takes up defence -- the defence of the country shall be considered a member of the armed forces, all obligations apply both to that individual as well as to the commander and these provisions are repeated afterwards. So -- but the key issue is really to look at the specific documents because without running too far -- but there example in Sector East where members of local armed groups, when I say Sector East I mean Slavonia, Baranja -- Eastern Slavonia -- sorry, Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, there are a number of instances where armed individuals are operating in group and there is no mention made of the JNA, and as an analyst I would like to see any documents discussing that area at that time to see whether -- who is in command there because maybe the JNA isn't there anymore and then the picture, of course, looks totally different.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So the issue is whether or not they are present in a zone of responsibility; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that is one of the important issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And how do we know whether or not a zone of responsibility is in existence -- sorry, or an area of responsibility, zone or area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: By looking at the specific military documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's go to one then.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 422, Prosecution tab 117, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, this is -- you've looked at this document either today or yesterday, and this is from Panic, commander of the 1st Military District, dated the 15th of October to subordinate commands, as well as the provincial TO staff of the autonomous province of Vojvodina. And this document says: "Pursuant to recent problems in the zones of combat activities and with the aim of regulating the life, work, order, and discipline, I hereby order: "1. Establish full control in the AOR of the units ..." Let's just stop there, is AOR an acronym for area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah -- I mean, this is not the original B/C/S because I know that in another case I had -- one of my colleagues was testifying. This is a long time ago. There was a quite deep debate with the Defence about whether it was an area or a zone of responsibility. And so when you look in the B/C/S it says -- sorry, I touched the screen, it says "zona" or "zoni," "ogdgovornosti," that is why I used the term "zone of responsibility" but it corresponds to the same concept. Yes, indeed. I mean, to answer your question the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And -- well, let's just pin that down. So there is no difference between the concept of area of responsibility and zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, area of responsibility was not used, I mean the concept of area of responsibility was not used by the JNA. It's called zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you. And then the remainder of the provision says: "Pay special attention to the functioning of the military authority in all the settlements and do not permit the local organs of authority to interfere and exert influence until the civilian control of the liberated territory is established." Now, just that last bit is what I would like to ask you to focus on. Would you agree that Panic's view is that this zone of responsibility is going to continue until, as he puts it, civilian control of the liberated territory is established; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, maybe I would word it differently because the concept of -- I mean, the concept -- it is obviously the zone of responsibility of the 1st Military District and its subordinate units, but what Panic is basically saying, that is, that the JNA remains responsible in the area and has to control all aspects because at that time there is no official view on whether or not -- sorry, there is no official view on which attitude to adopt towards the self-declared SAO SBWS organs of authority. And it's only on the 20th of November as we saw with I think it was 26 -- sorry, with 2436-1 that the 1st Military District recognised the SAO SBWS authorities as competent authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We're going to discuss extensively that thesis, which I suggest to you is quite wrong. But the last point that I want to make or question that I would like to ask you is who in your view, reading this document, is going to determine whether or not civilian control has been established? Who is that up to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Panic actually doesn't explain it here. And when we look at the other documents, that is basically -- I mean, he at one moment, around the 20th of November, he must have received instructions from his commander, i.e., from the SSNO, when I use "must," it is because I haven't seen the specific document, but on the 20th of November there is a change in the instructions from the 1st Military District towards subordinate units in relation to the attitude they have to adopt towards SAO SBWS organs of authority. And then we see later on 25th of November and early December we see the more specific instructions, 588-1 and 588-3, from the SSNO. So it has to come from a superior military authority. Whether anything was decided on the political level, I don't know, I haven't seen the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, if you don't mind, we would call it a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Theunens, we will see you again tomorrow at 9.00. And as I told you the two previous days, don't discuss your testimony with anybody, don't talk to any of the parties. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian, how far are -- is OTP with witness planning and practical arrangements for witnesses? And I ask you this with regard to the 27th of May when there is a ceremony at the Tribunal and where we have been asked eventually to consider not to sit that day. Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That is a very good question. We currently have the financial expert scheduled for the 27th and the 28th. If the Trial Chamber is inclined not to sit that day, then I think we can perhaps do some reshuffling, but that was the current plan to call the financial expert on the 27th and the 28th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll let you know. Thank you very much. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 10th day of May, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.01 p.m.,
